### 2026-06-03-1468-triage-audit-reconcile: triage: reconcile/self-heal audit log from proposed/pending/active vBRIEF inventory (#1468)  `[completed]`

The triage audit log xbrief/.eval/candidates.jsonl is the single source of truth for 'has issue #N been triaged?', yet it can silently desync from the ingested vBRIEF inventory in xbrief/proposed/ / pending/ / active/. The audit log is operator-private and gitignored (sibling #1464), so branch churn or a xbrief/.eval/ cleanup can wipe it without git noticing. Bootstrap backfill (scripts/triage_bootstrap.py::step_backfill_audit_log) is point-in-time only: it writes one accept per vBRIEF present at the instant it runs and skips issue numbers already logged, so later-ingested vBRIEFs are never re-backfilled. The net effect is that a proposed/pending/active vBRIEF for #N carrying a valid x-xbrief/github-issue reference but no accept decision in the log is an internally inconsistent state that triage:summary faithfully (but confusingly) counts as untriaged, with no discoverable repair path short of a full task triage:bootstrap re-run (which also re-fetches the cache). This scope adds a discoverable, idempotent self-heal: a new `task triage:reconcile` verb that derives the missing accept decisions from the on-disk vBRIEF inventory without a cache re-fetch, plus a `[triage:reconcile] N` divergence hint emitted by triage:summary (mirroring the existing [triage:scope] line) so the operator is pointed at the repair verb. Coordinates with #1464: because the audit log is silently wipeable, the filesystem vBRIEF inventory must remain a recoverable source for lost accept decisions.

**Acceptance**:

- A consumer whose candidates.jsonl is reset/lost can recover full triage state from the on-disk vBRIEF inventory via a single, discoverable repair verb (no manual JSONL editing, no full cache re-fetch required). `[proposed]`
- task triage:summary does not report an issue as untriaged when a proposed/pending/active vBRIEF for it exists with a valid x-xbrief/github-issue reference (either via self-heal or via a surfaced reconcile hint). `[proposed]`
- Regression coverage: reset the audit log to a single backfill entry while N proposed/ vBRIEFs exist; assert the reconcile path restores N accept decisions and the summary untriaged count returns to 0. `[proposed]`

### 2026-06-03-1474-deftcheck-runs-framework-self-tests-in-consumers-always-red: deft:check runs framework self-tests in consumers (always-red gate; 14 failed + 6 errors by construction)  `[completed]`

## Summary

In a vendored consumer install, `task deft:check` delegates to the framework's own check (`.deft/core/Taskfile.yml`), which runs the **framework's full pytest self-test suite** under `.deft/core/tests/`. Many of those tests assert on artifacts that only exist in the framework's own repo (`deftai/directive`), so they **fail by construction in any consumer checkout** — producing a wall of red that is pure noise to the consumer and buries any real, consumer-relevant check failures.

Net effect: `task deft:check` can never be green in a consumer, so the consumer-facing quality gate is unusable as a pass/fail signal and every consumer PR must invoke the review-cycle skill's pre-existing-failure carve-out.

Sibling to #1463 / #1464 / #1465 / #1468 (framework runtime behavior that misbehaves in the vendored consumer layout).

## Observed live in `deftai/statusreport`

`task deft:check` on a clean consumer checkout (vendored framework v0.39.7):

```
6823 passed, 14 failed, 6 errors, 4 skipped, 9 deselected, 1 xfailed
```

All 14 failures + 6 errors are framework self-tests under `.deft/core/tests/`. Categories:

- Tests asserting framework CI workflow files exist — e.g. `.deft/core/.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.deft/core/.github/workflows/branch-gate.yml` (not shipped in the vendored payload).
- Tests asserting the framework's own docs exist — e.g. `test_eval_readme_documents_policy` checks `.deft/core/xbrief/.eval/README.md` (a framework-repo file; the consumer's bootstrap writes the README at repo-root `xbrief/.eval/README.md` instead).
- Version-resolution tests expecting a dev/older version but getting the pinned release `0.39.7`.

Proven pre-existing + path-independent (consumer-side): stashing an unrelated consumer doc edit and re-running still reproduces the same failures. Tracked consumer-side in `deftai/statusreport#12`.

## Root cause

The committed `.deft/core/` payload (#11) ships the framework's **own test suite**, and the consumer-facing `task deft:check` runs it. Those tests were written to validate the framework *in its own repo* and depend on framework-repo-only artifacts (CI workflows, the framework's `xbrief/.eval/README.md`, the framework's dev version string). There is no "am I running inside the framework repo vs. a vendored consumer?" guard, and no consumer-scoped check target that runs only consumer-relevant validation.

## Gaps

- The vendored payload includes `.deft/core/tests/` (framework self-tests) and exposes them through the consumer `deft:check` path.
- No consumer-vs-framework execution-context detection to skip framework-repo-only tests when running outside `deftai/directive`.
- No separate consumer-scoped check target (lint/fmt/typecheck + consumer content validation such as vbrief validate / spec render) distinct from the framework's self-test suite.
- The review-cycle and pre-pr skills mandate "task check passes," which is unsatisfiable in a consumer without the carve-out — so the gate is effectively always bypassed.

## Suggested fix (directive)

Pick one or combine:

1. **Don't ship framework self-tests to consumers.** Exclude `.deft/core/tests/` (and any framework-repo-only fixtures) from the installer/relocator payload deposit so the consumer never runs them.
2. **Scope `task deft:check` for consumers.** Make the consumer-facing check run only consumer-relevant checks (lint/fmt/typecheck + `vbrief:validate` / spec render / governance), and move the framework's pytest suite behind a framework-dev-only target (e.g. `task deft:selftest`).
3. **Context-guard the self-tests.** Have framework-repo-only tests `skip`/`xfail` when an execution-context probe detects a vendored consumer (e.g. absence of `.deft/core/.github/` or a `deftai/directive`-repo marker), so a stray run is clean rather than red.

## Acceptance criteria

- On a fresh vendored consumer install with valid consumer content, `task deft:check` exits 0 (no framework-self-test failures/errors).
- Framework-repo-only tests are either not shipped to consumers or skip cleanly outside the framework's own repo.
- Real consumer-relevant failures (lint, vbrief validation, spec render) are still surfaced and still fail the check.
- Regression coverage: a consumer-layout fixture asserts `deft:check` is green when consumer content is valid and red when a consumer-relevant check actually fails.

---
Related: #11 (committed `.deft/core/` payload), the `no-mixed-core-and-app` guard, the review-cycle pre-existing-failure carve-out (`skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md` Phase 2 Step 3). Consumer-side tracker: `deftai/statusreport#12`. Sibling consumer-layout bugs: #1463, #1464, #1465, #1468.

**Acceptance**:

- On a fresh vendored consumer install with valid consumer content, task deft:check exits 0 (no framework-self-test failures/errors). `[proposed]`
- Framework-repo-only tests are either not shipped to consumers or skip cleanly outside the framework's own repo. `[proposed]`
- Real consumer-relevant failures (lint, vbrief validation, spec render) are still surfaced and still fail the check. `[proposed]`
- Regression coverage: a consumer-layout fixture asserts task deft:check is green when consumer content is valid and red when a consumer-relevant check actually fails. `[proposed]`

### 2026-06-03-1475-task-check-type-check-parity-with-ci-run-mypy-over-tests-not: task check: type-check parity with CI (run mypy over tests/, not just run.py)  `[completed]`

## Problem

Local `task check` is **not at type-check parity with CI**, so a mypy error that lives outside `run.py`'s import closure escapes every local pre-merge gate and breaks `master` for everyone after merge.

This happened for real this cycle:

- PR #1466 (issue #1465) passed `task check` locally and merged green, but immediately turned `master`'s **"Python (lint + type-check + test)"** job RED.
- Root cause: a mypy error in `tests/cli/test_behavioral_events.py` — a binding named `ignored` was first a `CompletedProcess[str]` and then reassigned to `list[str]`.
- CI runs `mypy tests/` (broad scope); local `core:lint` / `task check` only runs `mypy run.py`. The error was invisible locally and to every dispatched worker.
- It required an emergency one-line hotfix (PR #1472) and forced re-syncs across the in-flight cohort (#1463 / #1464 / #1468), each of which had inherited the red `tests/` file by merging `master`.

## Impact

- Any mypy error under `tests/` (or anywhere outside `run.py`'s import graph) ships green locally and breaks `master` post-merge.
- In a swarm/worktree workflow this is amplified: every concurrent branch that merges `master` inherits the red state and must re-sync after the hotfix.

## Proposed fix

- Expand the local type-check gate (`core:lint` / `task check`) to run mypy over the **same target set CI uses** — at minimum `mypy tests/`, ideally the whole tree (`mypy .` or the configured packages).
- Ensure the mypy configuration (pyproject / mypy.ini) is shared between local and CI so scope and strictness match.
- Make the broader scope **fail** `task check` (not advisory).

## Acceptance criteria

- `task check` (or `core:lint`) runs mypy with the same scope as the CI "Python (lint + type-check + test)" job, including `tests/`.
- A deliberately introduced type error under `tests/` causes `task check` to FAIL locally.
- Any docs/comments that describe the lint/type-check scope are updated to reflect parity.

## References

- Introduced by: PR #1466 (#1465)
- Hotfix: PR #1472
- Cohort affected by the inherited red: #1463, #1464, #1468

**Acceptance**:

- task check (or core:lint) runs mypy with the same scope as the CI "Python (lint + type-check + test)" job, including tests/. `[proposed]`
- A deliberately introduced type error under tests/ causes task check to FAIL locally. `[proposed]`
- Any docs/comments that describe the lint/type-check scope are updated to reflect parity. `[proposed]`

### 2026-06-03-1476-bugtriagecache-closed-upstream-issues-remain-in-triagequeue: bug(triage,cache): closed upstream issues remain in triage:queue when cached open entries are TTL-fresh  `[completed]`

## Summary

`task triage:queue` can surface closed upstream GitHub issues as actionable `[untriaged]` work when the local cache still says the issue is open. The failure mode survives `task cache:fetch-all -- --source=github-issue --repo deftai/directive` because the fetch defaults to `state=open`; once an issue closes upstream it is no longer enumerated, so its cached `raw.json` is never rewritten to `state=closed`. The cache entry can remain "fresh" for its 7-day TTL, and `task verify:cache-fresh` can still pass because it checks the newest in-scope `fetched_at`, not every queue candidate's live state.

This is a queue correctness bug, separate from #1424's queue-speed/N+1 issue.

## Observed live

After #1322 closed upstream:

- GitHub live state:
  - `gh api repos/deftai/directive/issues/1322 --jq '{state:.state,closed:.closed_at}'`
  - returned `state: closed`, `closed: 2026-06-03T02:07:37Z`
- Local cache state:
  - `.deft-cache/github-issue/deftai/directive/1322/raw.json` still had `"state": "open"`
  - `.deft-cache/github-issue/deftai/directive/1322/meta.json` had:
    - `fetched_at: 2026-06-01T17:09:02Z`
    - `expires_at: 2026-06-08T17:09:02Z`
    - `ttl_seconds: 604800`
- After `task cache:fetch-all -- --source=github-issue --repo deftai/directive`, the report showed many `already_fresh` / `skipped` entries and the queue still ranked #1322.
- `task triage:queue -- --limit=10` continued to show:
  - `[untriaged] #1322 deft-install ... (label: adoption-blocker)`
- `task verify:cache-fresh` passed:
  - `✓ deft cache-fresh: deftai/directive -- 175 entry/ies in scope; newest fetched 0.0h ago ...`

The operator had to manually notice that #1322 was closed and correct the recommendation.

## Root-cause sketch

From the current code:

- `scripts/triage_queue.py::load_cached_issues()` excludes closed issues only when cached `raw.json` has `state != "open"`:
  - stale `raw.json` with `"state": "open"` still enters the queue.
- `scripts/cache.py::cache_fetch_all()` defaults `state="open"` and delegates to `_cache_fetch.run_fetch_all()`.
- `scripts/_cache_fetch.py::run_fetch_all()` enumerates `rest_issue_list_paginated(repo, state=state, limit=limit)`.
  - closed upstream issues are absent from the default open-only enumeration, so already-cached entries that closed upstream are not revisited.
  - even `--state=all` would likely skip a still-TTL-fresh entry unless there is a force/invalidation path, because `_is_fresh(meta.json)` gates `do_put`.
- `scripts/preflight_cache.py::evaluate()` computes freshness from the max/newest `fetched_at` among scoped entries.
  - A fresh newly-fetched issue can make the gate pass while older cached queue candidates remain stale and wrong.

## Expected behavior

The queue's answer to "what should I work on next?" MUST NOT include upstream-closed issues as actionable untriaged work.

At least one of these should become true:

1. `task triage:queue` excludes or warns on candidates whose cached entry is stale enough that live state may have changed, especially top-ranked candidates.
2. `task cache:fetch-all` has a state-refresh mode for previously-cached entries that are no longer returned by the open-issue enumeration.
3. `task cache:fetch-all --state=all` or a new `--force` / `--refresh-existing` mode rewrites still-TTL-fresh cached entries when the caller explicitly wants authoritative state.
4. `task verify:cache-fresh` fails or warns when ranked queue candidates have `fetched_at` older than the freshness window, even if another scoped entry was fetched recently.

The exact implementation is open, but the operator-facing invariant is not: closed upstream issues should not rank as work.

## Acceptance criteria

- Reproduce with a cached issue whose `raw.json` says `state=open`, whose upstream GitHub issue is now closed, and whose cache `expires_at` is still in the future.
- After the fix, `task triage:queue -- --limit=10` does not surface that issue as `[untriaged]` actionable work.
- A cache refresh path exists that can update already-cached entries to `state=closed` even when the default open-only enumeration no longer returns them.
- `task verify:cache-fresh` no longer gives a misleading all-clear when the queue can still rank stale closed candidates, or the queue performs its own defensive stale-state handling.
- Regression test covers the #1322 shape: closed upstream, cached open, TTL-fresh cache entry.

## Related

- #1119 — cache-as-operator-working-set umbrella
- #1128 — `triage:queue` / `triage:audit` / `triage:show`
- #1127 — `verify:cache-fresh`
- #1322 — observed stale candidate after upstream closure
- #1379 — related but broader multi-machine cache continuity; not a duplicate
- #1424 — queue/cache freshness performance issue; separate from this correctness gap

**Acceptance**:

- Reproduce with a cached issue whose raw.json says state=open, whose upstream GitHub issue is now closed, and whose cache expires_at is still in the future. `[proposed]`
- After the fix, task triage:queue -- --limit=10 does not surface that issue as [untriaged] actionable work. `[proposed]`
- A cache refresh path exists that can update already-cached entries to state=closed even when the default open-only enumeration no longer returns them. `[proposed]`
- task verify:cache-fresh no longer gives a misleading all-clear when the queue can still rank stale closed candidates, or the queue performs its own defensive stale-state handling. `[proposed]`
- Regression test covers the #1322 shape: closed upstream, cached open, TTL-fresh cache entry. `[proposed]`

### 2026-06-03-1477-wired-git-hooks-ship-non-executable-mode-100644-silently-ine: Wired git hooks ship non-executable (mode 100644) -- silently inert on Unix consumers (follow-up to #1463)  `[completed]`

## Summary

The git hooks wired by the installer (#1463) are deposited **non-executable (mode `100644`)**. On Linux/macOS, git **silently skips hooks that lack the executable bit**, so the branch-protection (`pre-commit`) and destructive-push (`pre-push`) gates that #1463 introduced **never fire for Unix consumers** — the feature is silently inert on exactly the platforms where the executable bit matters.

This is a follow-up defect to #1463 (consumer git hooks): the hooks are wired and `core.hooksPath` is set, but the files ship without `+x`.

## Observed live in `deftai/statusreport`

After upgrading the vendored framework to **v0.40.0** (which ships #1463's hook wiring), Greptile flagged it as **P1** on PR #15:

- `.githooks/pre-commit` (blob `423453a6`) and `.githooks/pre-push` (blob `25014016`) are committed at mode `100644`.
- These repo-root files are byte-identical mirrors (same blob SHAs) of the vendored payload `.deft/core/.githooks/*`, which are **also** `100644`.

(Note: this repo is on Windows, where the executable bit is moot — which is why it shipped unnoticed. The breakage is Unix-only.)

## Root cause

- The installer (`cmd/deft-install/githooks.go`, #1463) deposits/stages the hook files at `100644`.
- `task setup` only runs `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` — it does **not** `chmod +x` the hooks.

So both the deposited repo-root copies and the canonical payload copies lack the executable bit, and nothing in the install/setup path adds it.

## Impact

- On Linux/macOS consumers, `pre-commit` (branch-protection / `verify:branch` / encoding gate) and `pre-push` (destructive-gh-verb gate) **do not run** — commits to the default branch and the other guarded actions proceed ungated, silently.
- The protection appears installed (`core.hooksPath` is set, files exist) but is non-functional — a silent-failure security/governance gap.

## Suggested fix (directive)

- Stage/deposit `.githooks/*` (and the payload `.deft/core/.githooks/*`) with mode `100755` so the executable bit is preserved through the git-free file swap, **and/or**
- Have `task setup` / the installer `chmod +x` the hook files (and `git update-index --chmod=+x` for the tracked deposit) after wiring `core.hooksPath`.
- Add a `verify:hooks-installed` assertion that the resolved hooks are executable on POSIX (not just present), so a regression surfaces loudly.

## Acceptance criteria

- After a fresh install/upgrade on Linux/macOS, `.githooks/pre-commit` and `.githooks/pre-push` are executable and actually fire (a commit to the default branch is blocked by the branch gate).
- The tracked deposit records mode `100755` for the hook files, surviving a subsequent `--upgrade`.
- Regression coverage asserting POSIX executability of the wired hooks.

---
Follow-up to #1463 (consumer git hooks). Surfaced on `deftai/statusreport` PR #15 (v0.40.0 upgrade). Sibling consumer-layout bugs: #1464, #1465, #1468, #1474.

**Acceptance**:

- After a fresh install/upgrade on Linux/macOS, .githooks/pre-commit and .githooks/pre-push are executable and actually fire (a commit to the default branch is blocked by the branch gate). `[proposed]`
- The tracked deposit records mode 100755 for the hook files, surviving a subsequent --upgrade. `[proposed]`
- Regression coverage asserting POSIX executability of the wired hooks. `[proposed]`

### 2026-06-03-1478-deft-core-guard-allowlist-omits-githooks-blocks-every-consum: deft-core-guard allowlist omits .githooks/ -- blocks every consumer v0.40.0 upgrade PR (#1463 deposit vs #1430 guard out of sync)  `[completed]`

## Summary

v0.40.0's `deft-core-guard` ("no-mixed-core-and-app") **rejects every consumer upgrade PR** because its installer-managed allowlist does not exempt `.githooks/`, even though v0.40.0's installer (`githooks.go`, #1463) now deposits repo-root `.githooks/pre-commit` + `.githooks/pre-push` as part of the framework install. The guard sees `.deft/core/**` (payload) mixed with `.githooks/*` (classified as "app") and fails the PR.

This is a hard **adoption-blocker regression**: the #1463 hook deposit and the #1430/#1440 guard fell out of sync. Distinct from #1477 (hook executable mode); this one blocks the upgrade PR from merging at all.

## Observed live in `deftai/statusreport`

A clean `deft-install --yes --upgrade` to v0.40.0, committed framework-only (the installer pre-staged exactly its managed paths), still fails `deft-core-guard` on the resulting PR:

```
##[error]This PR changes the vendored framework payload (.deft/core/**) AND non-framework files. Split the framework update into its own PR.
--- non-framework changes ---
.githooks/pre-commit
.githooks/pre-push
```

Those two files are the *only* members of the "app" set; everything else is either `.deft/core/**` or already allowlisted.

## Root cause

In `cmd/deft-install/deposit.go`, `installerManagedMatchers()` (the single source of truth feeding both the deposited guard ERE and the Go classifier) lists `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/`, `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`, `greptile.json`, the codeql config, the guard workflow, and vbrief scaffolding — but **not `.githooks/`**. Meanwhile `githooks.go` (#1463) deposits repo-root `.githooks/pre-commit` + `.githooks/pre-push`. So a legitimate `--upgrade` PR that includes the hook deposit is rejected by construction.

Compounding: the installer **skips updating an existing `.github/workflows/deft-core-guard.yml`**, so even once the allowlist is fixed upstream, already-installed consumers won't receive the corrected guard on a subsequent `--upgrade` unless the installer re-deposits/refreshes it.

## Suggested fix (directive)

- Add `{prefix: ".githooks/"}` to `installerManagedMatchers()` so both the deposited guard regex (`installerManagedGuardERE`) and the Go classifier (`classifyChangedPaths`) exempt the hook deposit.
- Refresh the deposited `deft-core-guard.yml` on `--upgrade` (or version it) so existing consumers pick up allowlist changes instead of keeping a stale guard.
- Add regression coverage in the `classifyChangedPaths` / `guardWouldFail` tests asserting `.githooks/pre-commit` and `.githooks/pre-push` are installer-managed (not "app").

## Acceptance criteria

- A consumer `--upgrade` PR that deposits `.githooks/*` alongside `.deft/core/**` passes `deft-core-guard`.
- Existing consumers receive the corrected guard workflow on their next `--upgrade` (not skipped).
- Tests pin `.githooks/` as installer-managed in the guard classifier.

---
Found on `deftai/statusreport` PR #15 (v0.40.0 upgrade). Related: #1463 (consumer git hooks deposit), #1477 (hooks ship non-executable), #1430 / #1440 (deft-core-guard + installer-managed allowlist).

**Acceptance**:

- A consumer --upgrade PR that deposits .githooks/* alongside .deft/core/** passes deft-core-guard. `[proposed]`
- Existing consumers receive the corrected guard workflow on their next --upgrade (not skipped). `[proposed]`
- Tests pin .githooks/ as installer-managed in the guard classifier. `[proposed]`

### 2026-06-03-1487-swarm-deft-directive-swarm-must-complete-the-cohort-vbrief-l: swarm: deft-directive-swarm must complete the cohort vBRIEF lifecycle (active -> completed) on swarm close  `[completed]`

## Summary

When the `deft-directive-swarm` skill finishes a cohort (all worker PRs merged), the cohort's story vBRIEFs are left in `xbrief/active/` -- they are never moved to `xbrief/completed/`. The swarm skill should OWN this lifecycle cleanup as part of its completion (Phase 5 "Complete vBRIEFs" / Phase 6 "Close"), so a completed swarm leaves no stories stranded in `active/`.

Observed in the 2026-06-03 swarm: after PR #1484 merged all 8 stories, the 8 child story vBRIEFs remained in `xbrief/active/` and their decompose-created epic parents remained in `xbrief/pending/`. Nothing in the swarm flow swept them to `completed/`.

## Why this is swarm-skill cleanup (not a one-off chore)

This is a recurring gap, not specific to one cohort: every swarm run that decomposes issues into stories leaves the same residue unless the skill cleans up on completion. The skill's Phase 5 "Complete vBRIEFs" step (`task scope:complete` per story) and Phase 6 "Close" already describe completing vBRIEFs, but the headless / multi-worker path did not execute the sweep for the cohort. The skill needs an explicit, reliable completion sweep wired into swarm close.

## Interaction with #1485 (must fix first)

Naively running `task scope:complete` (active -> completed) RE-BREAKS the D4 parent/child linkage, because `scope:complete` moves the child file without updating the parent epic's reference -- the exact bug tracked in #1485. So this work is BLOCKED ON #1485: once lifecycle moves update decomposed-parent back-references, the swarm skill can safely sweep cohort stories active -> completed (and complete/close the now-childless epic parents) while keeping `task vbrief:validate` green.

## Scope

- Add an explicit completion sweep to `deft-directive-swarm` (Phase 6 Close, after the merge cascade): for each fully-merged cohort story, `task scope:complete` the `active/` child; reconcile/complete the decompose-created epic parent once all its children are complete.
- Ensure the sweep keeps `task vbrief:validate` green (depends on #1485).
- Cover BOTH the interactive and the headless / multi-worker launch paths.
- Immediate residue: sweep the 8 stranded 2026-06-03 cohort stories (#1114 #1115 #1420 #1474 #1475 #1476 #1477 #1478) from `active/` -> `completed/` (and their epic parents from `pending/`) once #1485 lands.

## Acceptance criteria

- After a swarm cohort's PRs merge, no cohort story vBRIEFs remain in `xbrief/active/`; each is in `xbrief/completed/` with status `completed`.
- The decompose-created epic parents are completed/closed once their children are complete.
- `task vbrief:validate` is green after the sweep (no D4 linkage regressions).
- The `deft-directive-swarm` SKILL documents the completion sweep as a required Phase 6 step.

Suggested labels: process, agent-experience. Blocked by #1485. Refs #1484.

**Acceptance**:

- After a swarm cohort's PRs merge, no cohort story vBRIEFs remain in `xbrief/active/`; each is in `xbrief/completed/` with status `completed`. `[proposed]`
- The decompose-created epic parents are completed/closed once their children are complete. `[proposed]`
- `task vbrief:validate` is green after the sweep (no D4 linkage regressions). `[proposed]`
- The `deft-directive-swarm` SKILL documents the completion sweep as a required Phase 6 step. `[proposed]`

### 2026-06-03-1488-rfc-demote-the-1000-line-file-cap-from-must-to-should-unenfo: RFC: demote the 1000-line file cap from MUST to SHOULD (unenforced, self-violated, anti-deep-modules)  `[completed]`

## Summary

The 1000-line file cap is currently encoded as an RFC2119 `MUST` (`coding/coding.md:43`, `coding/coding.md:202`), but it is **unenforced**, **routinely violated by our own production code**, and **in tension with the framework's own "deep modules" architecture goal**. An unenforced, widely-broken `MUST` erodes the authority of every other `MUST` in the framework.

This issue proposes demoting the hard per-file line cap to a `SHOULD`/review-trigger and keeping cohesion (one responsibility per file) as the real hard rule.

## Where the rule lives

```
- ~ Files <300 lines ideal; files <500 lines recommended; ! files <1000 lines maximum   (coding/coding.md:43)
- ⊗ Files over 1000 lines                                                                (coding/coding.md:202)
```

Note: `pyproject.toml:78-80` attributes the cap to "deft/main.md", but `main.md` does not actually state it — the rule lives only in `coding/coding.md`. `coding/hygiene.md` (the ongoing-codebase-health doc) never mentions file size at all.

## Evidence

### 1. We don't obey our own MUST (dogfooding failure)

24 Python files exceed 1000 lines; **12 are production source** under `scripts/`:

- `scripts/migrate_vbrief.py` — 2,589 (2.6x the cap)
- `scripts/doctor.py` — 2,217
- `scripts/release.py` — 2,027
- `scripts/triage_help.py` — 1,684
- `scripts/triage_queue.py` — 1,139
- `scripts/triage_bootstrap.py` — 1,085
- `scripts/vbrief_validate.py` — 1,083
- `scripts/reconcile_issues.py` — 1,063
- `scripts/relocate.py` — 1,030
- `scripts/cache.py` — 1,021
- `scripts/issue_ingest.py` — 1,017
- `scripts/triage_summary.py` — 1,011

(The remaining 12 are test files, e.g. `tests/cli/test_migrate_vbrief.py` at 2,954.)

`pyproject.toml:76-80` even documents a workaround (`combine-as-imports = true`) introduced specifically to keep `migrate_vbrief.py` "under the 1000-line MUST limit." That file is now 2.6x over — the workaround failed and the rule was never enforced.

### 2. It is enforced nowhere

- `ruff` config (`pyproject.toml:72-73`) selects no module-length rule (no `PLR0915`, no pylint `C0302`).
- `scripts/doctor.py` has no line-count check.
- The `deft-directive-pre-pr` skill has no file-size check.
- No `task` target checks it.

The cap relies entirely on agent goodwill.

### 3. It violates our own Rule Authority axiom

`main.md:50-58` (Rule Authority [AXIOM]): *"Every rule MUST use the strongest applicable layer. Order: deterministic > Taskfile > vBRIEF > RFC2119 > prose."* A line count is trivially deterministic, so encoding it as RFC2119 prose is itself an axiom violation. Either enforce it deterministically or stop calling it a `MUST`.

### 4. It is in tension with our "deep modules" goal

The `deft-directive-gh-arch` skill is explicitly about "deepen shallow modules." A hard per-file line cap pressures contributors toward the shallow-module fragmentation (Ousterhout's "classitis") that this skill — and good architecture — warns against. Line count is a weak proxy; the real rule is one line above at `coding/coding.md:42`: `! One responsibility per file/module`.

## Industry context

- Linters that cap file length ship the rule as a **warning with per-file opt-outs**, not a build-breaking error (pylint `max-module-lines` default 1000 — likely our origin; ESLint `max-lines` default 300; Checkstyle `FileLength` default 2000; SonarQube treats it as a "code smell").
- Empirical evidence linking file size to defects is weak and confounded by total code volume; LOC is a poor quality metric and no study establishes 1000 as meaningful.
- Mature teams cap **function length / cyclomatic complexity** far more often than whole files, and optimize for **cohesion**, not raw line count.

The mainstream position: a 1000-line `MUST` is stricter than the tools that inspired it, unsupported by evidence, and architecturally counterproductive.

## Recommendations

### Option A (recommended) — demote to a SHOULD heuristic

- `coding/coding.md:43` → `~ files <300 ideal, <500 recommended, <1000 a review trigger — split when exceeded unless the file is genuinely single-responsibility`
- `coding/coding.md:202` → reframe the anti-pattern from "Files over 1000 lines" to "Large multi-responsibility files (size is a trigger to check cohesion, not an automatic defect)"
- Keeps the load-bearing `MUST` ("one responsibility per file"); makes size advisory.
- Zero code changes required; the codebase becomes immediately honest about the rule.
- Update the stale `pyproject.toml:76-80` comment (drop the "MUST limit" / "deft/main.md" references).

### Option B — keep the MUST but make it real (per the axiom)

- Add a deterministic line-count check wired into `task check` (and/or `doctor.py` / pre-pr).
- Bring the 12 production offenders into compliance by splitting, OR record documented exemptions (generated/aggregator files) with justification.
- More work, and arguably overkill given cohesion — not line count — is the actual goal.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decision is recorded (Option A, Option B, or a documented alternative).
- If Option A: `coding/coding.md:43`, `coding/coding.md:202`, and the `pyproject.toml` comment are updated; content tests referencing the cap (if any) are updated.
- If Option B: a deterministic check exists and passes, and either all offenders are split or each has a recorded exemption.

## References

- `coding/coding.md:42-43`, `coding/coding.md:202`
- `coding/hygiene.md` (no file-size rule)
- `main.md:50-58` (Rule Authority axiom)
- `pyproject.toml:72-80`
- `deft-directive-gh-arch` skill (deep modules)

**Acceptance**:

- A decision is recorded (Option A, Option B, or a documented alternative). `[proposed]`
- If Option A: `coding/coding.md:43`, `coding/coding.md:202`, and the `pyproject.toml` comment are updated; content tests referencing the cap (if any) are updated. `[proposed]`
- If Option B: a deterministic check exists and passes, and either all offenders are split or each has a recorded exemption. `[proposed]`

### 2026-06-04-1419-rfc-agentic-prioritization-coordination-model-for-deft-direc: RFC: Agentic Prioritization & Coordination Model for Deft Directive  `[completed]`

# RFC: Agentic Prioritization & Coordination Model for Deft Directive

**Supersedes**: #987
**Status**: Draft for Discussion (rev 13)
**Date**: 2026-06-02

_Rev 11 folded in research-informed changes (review/autonomy, outcome loop, risk-tiered gates, cost overlay, drift, receipts). Rev 12 added the **cost-capture plan** (start collecting actuals now). Rev 13 grounds cost capture on the **Warp Enterprise Analytics API** (per-message `credit_charged` + `git_context` over both interactive and cloud runs), adds a `credits` cost field + `task capacity:cost-sync`, and makes the overlay two-tier (enterprise-grounded vs estimate-only); warpdotdev/warp#12075 is narrowed to sub-enterprise access + raw token/$ exposure. Open Questions v2 tracks loosened items; full revision history is in the GitHub edit log._

## Context & Problem Statement
#987 identified that there is no first-class, sustainable way to express ordering or priority *between* separate vBRIEFs for swarm allocation and ROADMAP rendering. Today this is emergent: alphabetical filename order, selective promotion to `active/`, and operator judgment at allocation time. These are workable at current scale but fragile as agentic velocity rises, and per-item "urgent" work systematically displaces important-but-non-urgent work, accelerating debt.

This RFC proposes a durable model that (a) answers #987's concrete ordering gap, and (b) adds capacity protection and judgment gates so high-velocity agentic work doesn't quietly starve debt paydown or bypass human judgment on sensitive changes. Research note: the dominant industry failure mode is the *operating model*, not tooling (2025 DORA: throughput rises while stability slips); the bottleneck has shifted from execution to **human judgment/review capacity**. This RFC is an operating-model artifact and rev 11+ make the outflow side (review capacity, outcome quality, cost) first-class, not just the inflow side.

## Definitions of Debt Types
- **Technical Debt** — suboptimal code/architecture that raises the cost/risk of future change.
- **Cognitive Debt** — erosion of shared human understanding when the rate of (often agent-produced) change outpaces the team's ability to maintain a coherent mental model.
- **Agentic Debt (Orchestration Debt)** — brittle prompts/orchestration, unowned eval harnesses, tool-schema drift, context-management issues, and the growing agent-infrastructure surface that must be governed.

These are distinct. v1 buckets cognitive + agentic together; **context/doc drift** is the emerging measurable signal that could graduate cognitive debt to its own bucket (see Deferred to v2 + Open Questions v2).

## Goals
- Define a sustainable model for priority, ordering, and coordination between vBRIEFs.
- Make human judgment explicit and first-class where it adds value; keep it minimal on small projects.
- Treat human-clearance capacity, outcome quality, and cost as first-class, not just execution effort.
- Support brownfield and greenfield adoption without disruptive migrations.
- Work across scales (solo → multi-team).
- Prefer conventions/skills/metadata over vBRIEF schema changes.

## Non-Goals
- A universal numeric priority field every vBRIEF must maintain.
- Heavy ceremony on small projects.
- Fully automating prioritization (or human judgment) away.
- Replacing lightweight mechanisms that still work.
- A full agent control-plane (identity/SIEM/observability beyond decisions); deft's existing gate stack owns that.

## Guiding Principles
- **Reuse before invent.** Express new behavior through existing machinery (`plan.policy`, the `triageAutoClassify` match engine, `wipCap`, `triageRankingLabels`, the `verify:*` deterministic-gate pattern, the policy audit-row pattern, `migrate:vbrief`, the review-cycle skill, `deft-directive-cost`).
- **vBRIEF-canonical, SCM-agnostic.** The vBRIEF is the source of truth; SCM labels are an optional one-way mirror. Everything reads filesystem-truth and runs offline.
- **Deterministic enforcement.** Per the Rule Authority [AXIOM], anything load-bearing graduates from prose to a script gate wired into `task check` / hooks — or it erodes (cf. #798 / #954 / #1369).
- **Close the loop.** Inflow (what/how-much/order) is governed alongside outflow (review capacity, outcome quality, cost, earned autonomy).
- **Human judgment scales down gracefully**; auditable and explainable by default.

## Proposed Direction
Three orthogonal layers, all declared at the PROJECT-DEFINITION level:

1. **Capacity Allocation** — *how much* effort per category (protected buckets), measured over the completion flow + outcome & cost overlays.
2. **Judgment Gates** — *what must be human-cleared* before promotion/dispatch (risk-tiered).
3. **Selection Ordering** — *which ready item next* (the #987 answer + continuation precedence).

Cross-cutting: **Session-Start Nudge Budgeting** keeps surfaces quiet; **Review, Autonomy & Human-Clearance Capacity** governs the outflow side; **Brownfield Backfill** makes adoption painless.

### Layer 1 — Capacity Allocation
Protected effort buckets bias what gets promoted/worked so debt categories aren't starved by urgent work. **Capacity measures effort distribution, not delivered value** — it tracks where effort went. Outcome/value and cost are measured separately (overlays) so they aren't conflated.

**Default buckets (v1):**

```json
"buckets": [
  { "id": "new-capability", "target": 0.50 },
  { "id": "technical-debt", "target": 0.20 },
  { "id": "agentic-debt",   "target": 0.15 },
  { "id": "urgent",         "target": 0.15 }
]
```

**Denominator (v1: vBRIEF count, filesystem-truth).** Capacity is measured as a count of scope vBRIEFs — the same unit `wipCap` already counts. `unit: "weighted"` (size→weight) and `unit: "cost"` (credit/$ per vBRIEF) are defined-but-deferred; v1 ships `vbrief-count` with cost surfaced as a reporting overlay (see Cost capture).

**`kind`-aware counting (epics).** Only `kind: "story"` is executable; epics/phases are containers:
- `kind == "story"` → count its weight.
- `kind in {epic, phase}` **with** children → count **0**; children counted directly.
- `kind in {epic, phase}` **without** children (undecomposed) → count `plan.metadata.estimatedChildren` (`defaultEpicEstimate`, default 3, when unset).

The epic estimate only affects the **forward** view; backward adherence counts real completed stories. Children inherit `capacityBucket` from the parent epic (via `planRef`). The same rule feeds `wipCap`.

**`estimatedChildren` lifecycle.** In-flight grooming metadata: set at `scope:promote`; refinement may update; **retired at `scope:decompose`**. Field presence is the groomed signal — *absent* counts via `defaultEpicEstimate` AND fires a "needs estimation" nudge; *present* goes stale only on time (`epicStalenessDays`, default 14).

**Stranded slices (partially-completed epics).** A feature whose first slice landed but whose mates never did is debt. The completed slice **keeps its bucket** (freeze holds). The debt is **forward-recognized**: a partially-completed epic dormant > `epicStrandedDays` (default 30) is flagged with a **trichotomy** — finish / cancel & remove (file removal as tech-debt) / accept & file a tech-debt vBRIEF.

**Accounting window (required).** *Forward* (in-flight `pending/`+`active/` vs target → biases promotion) and *backward* (completed over a trailing window vs target → the report). `window: { kind: "trailing-days" | "trailing-completed", value: N }` (default `trailing-days: 30`).

**Enforcement is flow-based, not snapshot-based (small-N reality).**
- `wipCap` governs **concurrency**; buckets govern **longitudinal mix** over the completion stream. Different axes.
- Targets are enforced against **completed work over the trailing window**, not the in-flight snapshot.
- Selection is **deficit-biased** at `scope:promote` and cohort-fill (`deficit = target − actual`), applied at cohort assembly so lumps self-correct.
- **`minSampleSize` guard** (default 20): below this many **classified** completions (carrying `capacityBucket` + `completedAt`), capacity is advisory and selection falls back to Layer-3 ordering + `wipCap`. Counting *classified* completions prevents pre-adoption history from falsely activating capacity (see Brownfield Backfill).

**Outcome signal (closing the loop).** Capacity is an *input* metric; pair it with an *outcome* metric so a bucket can't be "busy but failing" invisibly. A per-bucket **outcome health overlay** (does NOT change the allocation metric): the **revert/rework rate** — git reverts plus follow-up fix vBRIEFs that `reference` a completed vBRIEF — computed filesystem-truth over the same window. Optionally integrate an external code-health/coverage signal where available. Surfaced in `capacity:show`; sustained high rework is a Tier-2 nudge.

**Where running totals live (derived, not stored).** Tallies computed on demand from the lifecycle folders: backward from `xbrief/completed/` (frozen `capacityBucket` + `completedAt`), forward from `pending/`+`active/`. Deficit computed at decision time. Optional rebuildable cache in `xbrief/.eval/` only; never authoritative.

**Cost capture (rev 11 overlay; rev 12 capture plan; rev 13 Analytics-API grounding).** Agentic work has real, variable credit/$ cost; a count-based denominator can hide that one bucket is many times the spend of another. `capacity:show` surfaces a per-bucket **cost** column. Capture mechanics:
- **`plan.metadata.cost = { credits, tokens, usd, source, partial, asOf }`** is stamped on completed vBRIEFs whenever a figure is available — additive metadata that defaults absent, so projects **start collecting actuals now** and history accrues (you cannot backfill spend from git, so starting early matters — same logic as `completedAt`). `credits` is the native Warp unit; `usd` is derived via a configured credit→$ rate; `tokens` is populated only when a token-level source is available (the Warp Analytics API reports credits, not tokens).
- **Capture from telemetry, never agent self-report** (models can't accurately report their own usage). Primary source: the **Warp Enterprise Analytics API** (`/enterprises/analytics/events` + `/users`), which exposes per-message `credit_charged` over **both `local` interactive and `cloud` runs** — directly covering the surface that was previously a gap. Supplementary token-level sources where present: the model API `usage` field; CLI-harness OTEL/usage logs (Claude Code / Codex); the `oz` CLI / Oz API per-run usage.
- **Attribution — directive already owns the join key.** Analytics `events` rows carry `git_context.branch` + `head` and `conversation_id`; the swarm worktree flow assigns a known branch per story, so cost maps to a vBRIEF by branch/commit (fallback: `conversation_id` recorded at `scope:complete`). The `vBRIEF:` trailer / cohort manifest still splits a batched session across its stories; include review-cycle iterations, retries, and failed attempts (rework cost is signal, not noise).
- **Post-hoc sync (`task capacity:cost-sync`).** Analytics data lands minutes after a run (no inline figure), so a batch job queries `events` over the completion window, groups `credit_charged` by branch / `conversation_id`, and writes `cost` onto the matching completed vBRIEFs. Idempotent + re-runnable (same shape as `verify:*` / backfill). The same rows' `was_edited_by_user` / `code_changes` feed the outcome/rework overlay.
- **Provenance:** `source` (`warp-analytics-api` | `api-usage` | `harness-otel` | `platform` | `estimated`) + a `partial` flag (true when reviewer/cloud cost isn't captured), mirroring `capacityBucketSource`, so later analysis knows reliability.
- **Estimate-vs-actual calibration:** `deft-directive-cost` produces a pre-build estimate; these post-build actuals give estimate-vs-actual variance, which calibrates future estimates and is itself an outcome/health signal (a bucket whose actuals routinely exceed estimate is flagged).
- **Coverage is two-tier.** *Enterprise teams:* grounded for interactive + cloud via the Analytics API (admin-only; requires Admin Panel → Privacy *Enterprise Usage Reporting*). *Below enterprise (Pro/individual/non-admin):* no programmatic surface — cost stays **estimate-only** (`deft-directive-cost`) until per-task usage is exposed. Remaining upstream asks (sub-enterprise access; raw token/$ vs credits) tracked at **warpdotdev/warp#12075**. Promoting cost to a capacity `unit` is deferred (Open Questions v2).

**Bucket assignment (vBRIEF-canonical).** `plan.metadata.capacityBucket` (authoritative, SCM-neutral) + `plan.metadata.capacityBucketSource` (`match`|`agent`|`human`). Bucket `match` blocks only *propose*; human-confirmed wins. Unassigned → `defaultBucket`. **Re-bucketing** allowed in-flight, frozen at completion.

**`wipCap` reconciliation.** Hard ceiling; buckets are soft targets that bias selection. `advise` (default) deprioritizes over-target buckets + relief hint; `block` refuses over-target promotion with `--force`. A gate-blocked story still consumes its bucket's capacity (reserved); `capacity:show` shows a per-bucket `blocked` sub-count. **wipCap should be set relative to human-clearance throughput, not just machine concurrency** (see Review & Autonomy).

**Schema:**

```json
{ "plan": { "policy": { "capacityAllocation": {
  "unit": "vbrief-count",
  "window": { "kind": "trailing-days", "value": 30 },
  "enforcement": "advise",
  "minSampleSize": 20,
  "defaultBucket": "new-capability",
  "defaultEpicEstimate": 3,
  "epicStalenessDays": 14,
  "epicStrandedDays": 30,
  "finishBeforeStart": false,
  "buckets": [
    { "id": "new-capability", "target": 0.50, "match": { "labels": { "any-of": ["enhancement","feature"] } } },
    { "id": "technical-debt", "target": 0.20, "match": { "labels": { "any-of": ["tech-debt","refactor"] } } },
    { "id": "agentic-debt",   "target": 0.15, "match": { "labels": { "any-of": ["skills","orchestration","eval"] } } },
    { "id": "urgent",         "target": 0.15, "match": { "labels": { "any-of": ["urgent","blocks-release-tag"] } } }
  ]
} } } }
```

Validator: `sum(target) == 1.0` (±epsilon); unique ids; window present; `minSampleSize ≤ window.value` when `kind = "trailing-completed"`.

**Surfaces:** `task capacity:show` (target vs actual both views; per-bucket `blocked` sub-count, **outcome/rework rate**, **cost**; active/advisory mode line; full ranked nudge list; filesystem-truth, offline); a budgeted one-liner in `task triage:welcome`; `task verify:capacity` (three-state, advisory by default).

### Layer 2 — Judgment Gates (risk-tiered)
A judgment gate marks work that must be human-cleared before promotion to `active/` or dispatch. Orthogonal to priority.

**Reuse, don't reinvent.** Gates use the existing `triageAutoClassify` match DSL (`labels`, `body-text`, `state`, `age-days`) + a new `paths{any-of}` (glob) predicate, in `plan.policy.judgmentGates[]`.

```json
{
  "id": "secrets-and-credentials",
  "class": "mechanical",
  "match": {
    "labels":    { "any-of": ["area:secrets","security"] },
    "body-text": { "any-of": ["secret","credential","api key","token"] },
    "paths":     { "any-of": ["secrets/**","**/*.env","**/credentials*"] }
  },
  "tier": "block",
  "requiredHumanReviewers": 2,
  "reason": "touches secrets / credential handling -- requires human sign-off"
}
```

**Risk tiers, not binary.** Each gate carries a **tier** mapping to required human oversight ON TOP of automated multi-LLM review:
- `tier: "auto"` → automated multi-LLM review clearance suffices (0 human reviewers); annotate-only.
- `tier: "review"` → 1 human reviewer/clearance required.
- `tier: "block"` → 2-person review (+ threat-model for the highest-risk gates); hard-fail until cleared.

`requiredHumanReviewers` makes this explicit. Risk derives from surface area, sensitivity, blast radius, novelty; default-on safety gates default to `block`. Tiers compose with the autonomy dial (Review & Autonomy).

**Two gate classes.** `mechanical` (labels/body-text/paths): `secrets-and-credentials`, `production-infrastructure`, `agents-md-and-skills`, `installer-and-bootstrap`, `data-access-boundaries`, `financial-or-billing`, `high-risk-external-integrations`. `declared` (subjective, explicit tag): `core-orchestration`, `large-architectural-changes`, `compliance-and-audit`, `evaluation-and-safety`.

**`declared`-gate detection.** Tagged + no clearance → deterministic, honors tier. Untagged → advisory annotation only. Optional `paths` backstop. Mechanical gates fail-closed on detection; declared gates fail-open on omission.

**Default-on universal safety gates.** Hardcoded, default-on (`secrets-and-credentials`, `production-infrastructure`, `agents-md-and-skills`, `installer-and-bootstrap`); disabled only by explicit audited `judgmentGatesDisabled` or lowering the tier.

**Default `match` globs ("both, layered").** Framework ships portable Tier-A globs on universals; deft's own globs live in deft's PROJECT-DEFINITION. Consumers extend via additive union by `id`.

**SCM-agnostic tags.** `declared` tags live in `plan.metadata.judgmentGateTags[]` (filesystem-truth, offline). `match.labels` is GitHub-only behind `scripts/scm.py` (`verify:scm-boundary`, #1145).

**Two enforcement points.** (1) Promotion/allocation time — declared signals + `paths` vs `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope[]`. (2) PR time (omission-proof) — match the actual diff; an uncleared fired gate fails the PR check. Clearance binds to a `cleared_scope` fingerprint; scope creep re-triggers.

**Deterministic surface.** `scripts/verify_judgment_gates.py` → `task verify:judgment-gates`, three-state exit, wired into `task check` + `.githooks/pre-push` + a `judgment-gate` GH Actions workflow. Bypass `DEFT_ALLOW_UNGATED=1`. New `pathspec` matcher.

**Integration with the gate stack (#1378 / #1387).** `## Allocation context` gains `gate_clearances[]` (`{ gate_id, vbrief_path, cleared_by, rationale, cleared_at, cleared_scope }`). `task verify:story-ready` (Gate 0) fails on an uncleared active `block` gate. Headless `swarm:launch` (#1387): a gated story rides the consent token only if its clearance is pre-recorded.

**Multi-vBRIEF PR attribution.** Per-story checkpoint commits carry a `vBRIEF:` trailer → map commits to stories → partition diff → check per story. Path outside owning `file_scope[]` = scope creep; unattributable path hitting a `block` gate fails closed; runs pre-merge on unsquashed commits. v1 ships block-gated stories solo.

**Audit + precedence.** Clearances append to the durable audit log (see Receipts & Audit). First-match-wins (universals first); clearance per-gate-id.

### Layer 3 — Selection Ordering (the #987 answer + continuation precedence)
Capacity decides *how much*; Layer 3 decides *which ready item next*. Selection — in `task triage:queue` and swarm Phase 0 cohort-fill — is a lexicographic sort:

```
( urgent/blocking down, continuation down, bucket-deficit down, intra-bucket rank down, date up )
```

- **urgent/blocking** (highest) — `triageRankingLabels`; preempts everything incl. continuation.
- **continuation** — a story whose `planRef` parent epic has already *started* (≥1 child completed or sibling active). Outranks net-new single-issue work ("stop starting, start finishing"); oldest-started epic first; overrides the bucket deficit short-term by design.
- **bucket-deficit** — among net-new work, most-under-target bucket vs the trailing-window mix.
- **intra-bucket rank, then date** — `plan.metadata.rank` (vBRIEF-intrinsic mirror of `triageRankingLabels`), then creation date.

**Spec-readiness eligibility.** Only work that meets the swarm-readiness/spec-quality bar is promotable/selectable — under-specified work is refused with a pointer to `scope:decompose` / refinement ("bad spec = ×10 waste"); reuse the `task swarm:readiness` contract.

**Escape valve:** continuation precedence is safe because **cancel** exists. Optional hard variant `finishBeforeStart: true`: at/near `wipCap`, only continuation work is promotable.

Wiring `plan.metadata.rank` is still the smallest independently-shippable slice and closes #987.

## Review, Autonomy & Human-Clearance Capacity
The industry-wide lesson is that the bottleneck moved from execution to **human judgment/review capacity**. This RFC governs inflow; this section governs the outflow constraint.

**Automated review is the default first pass.** Line-level review is handled by automated multi-model LLM review (e.g. Greptile + a second-model reviewer via `deft-directive-review-cycle`). That scales and is NOT the human bottleneck.

**The scarce resource is human-clearance throughput** — merge approvals (swarm requires a human approval before the first merge), judgment-gate clearances, allocation/Phase-0 approvals, and adjudication when the LLM reviewers disagree or a reviewer errors/escalates.
- Surface a **pending-human-decisions backlog** in `capacity:show` and as a Tier-1 nudge when over threshold.
- `wipCap` SHOULD be tuned relative to clearance throughput, not just machine concurrency.

**Autonomy dial (Observe → Escalate → Execute).** The gate **tier** decides when automated multi-LLM clearance suffices vs human adjudication is required. An **autonomy level** (per project, optionally per gate-id) ratchets that line: advances as the clearance-override / false-positive rate stays low over a window (earned autonomy), reducing required human clearances; ratchets back on a spike in overrides or rework. Ratchet metric/thresholds → Open Question v2.

## Session-Start Nudge Budgeting
Capacity, gates, lifecycle hygiene, review, and cost each generate nudges. The session line is ruthlessly budgeted.

**Headline vs nudge (budget = 1).** `task triage:welcome` shows a state **headline** + **exactly one** primary nudge + a `+N more → task capacity:show` overflow. The full ranked list lives only in `capacity:show`.

**Ranking by rate-of-harm-accrual:**
- **Tier 1 (worsening):** stranded slice; gate-blocked-stuck bucket; urgent-bucket overrun; pending-human-decisions backlog over threshold.
- **Tier 2 (trending):** stale undecomposed epic; ungroomed in-flight epic; generic capacity skew; high per-bucket rework rate; cost-skew (a bucket dominating spend).
- **Tier 3 (informational):** advisory-mode (`sample < minSampleSize`); onboarding-incomplete; cache staleness.

Within a tier: magnitude → age → id. Same-class aggregated. **Tier-1 persists** (escalating wording; provisional); Tier 2/3 suppressed per-window. One shared ranking function backs `triage:welcome` + `capacity:show`.

## Brownfield Backfill (`task capacity:backfill`)
A pre-adoption project (including directive itself) is **classification cold-start**, not volume cold-start: several hundred completed vBRIEFs but none carry `capacityBucket`/`completedAt` and `kind` is partial. `minSampleSize` counts **classified** completions so unclassified history can't falsely activate capacity.

`task capacity:backfill` is a **one-time migration** (same shape as `task migrate:vbrief`):
- `completedAt` ← git landing time (deterministic, zero human).
- `kind` ← structural inference (items/references); agent for ambiguous.
- `capacityBucket` ← match rules → agent → **human reviews only the low-confidence batch**; records `capacityBucketSource`.
- in-flight epic `estimatedChildren` ← agent-proposed in the same pass.
- Note: historical **cost** actuals cannot be backfilled (no telemetry exists for past runs) — `cost` accrues only forward from adoption, which is why capture must start now.

Human job: confirm the 4 targets + skim the low-confidence batch. **Window-first** activation. **Dry-run-default** + `--apply` (atomic per file, idempotent + resumable, journaled, graceful degradation); **git is the wholesale undo** (+ `--rollback`); **post-backfill validation gate**. **Re-run is a safe no-op** (idempotency + completeness + the completion freeze); re-classification needs `--force --confirm` and never clobbers `human` buckets. **Cross-cutting dry-run convention:** `triage:queue` + `verify:judgment-gates` also offer `--dry-run`/preview.

## Receipts & Audit
Two tiers, reusing existing conventions (no new store):
- **Durable, committed audit** (`xbrief/.audit/*.jsonl`) — authority-bearing events: gate clearances, `--force` overrides, allocation approvals, autonomy-level changes. Record-of-record; append-only; must survive.
- **Gitignored telemetry** (`xbrief/.eval/`) — high-volume selection-ranking traces. Observability only; capped/rotatable; rebuildable since selection is deterministic.

## Agentic Pre-Grooming + Human Oversight
Agents handle pre-grooming (impact analysis, dedup, risk flagging, bucket/gate proposals, brownfield classification, first-pass review); humans retain final authority on allocation changes, gate clearances, target confirmation, merge approval, and high-context calls. Existing checkpoints (swarm Phase 0, #1378 Gate 0, review-cycle) are reused as the human-approval surface.

## Impact
- **vBRIEF schema:** no changes. New `plan.metadata` keys (`capacityBucket`, `capacityBucketSource`, `rank`, `estimatedChildren`, `weight`, `judgmentGateTags`, `completedAt`, `cost`); gate `tier`/`requiredHumanReviewers`; `plan.policy` arrays (`capacityAllocation`, `judgmentGates`, `judgmentGatesDisabled`) + an `autonomy` policy block.
- **Scripts/Taskfile:** `verify_judgment_gates.py`, `verify_capacity.py`, `capacity_show` (+ outcome/cost columns), `capacity_backfill`, `gate_clear`/`gate_show`; shared nudge-ranking function; deficit-biased selection + spec-readiness eligibility in `triage:queue`; `pathspec` matcher; `scope:promote` epic-aware branch; `scope:complete` stamps `completedAt` + `capacityBucket` + `cost` (when telemetry available); outcome (revert/rework) detector; cost capture via the Warp Analytics API / harness telemetry + a post-hoc `capacity:cost-sync` batch + `deft-directive-cost`.
- **Review/autonomy:** pending-human-decisions surface; autonomy-dial ratchet; gate tiers compose with the review-cycle skill.
- **Skills/renderers:** `deft-directive-triage`, `-refinement`, `-swarm`, `-review-cycle`, `-cost`; `roadmap_render.py` / `project_render.py` respect ordering + buckets.
- **Upstream dependency:** for **enterprise** teams, interactive + cloud cost capture is unblocked via the Warp Enterprise Analytics API (admin-only; requires the Privacy *Enterprise Usage Reporting* toggle). **warpdotdev/warp#12075** is narrowed to the remaining gaps: sub-enterprise (Pro/individual/non-admin) access and raw token/$ exposure (the API reports credits only).
- **Template propagation (#1309):** mirror into `templates/agents-entry.md` + extend `tests/content/test_agents_entry_contract.py`.

## Adoption Experience
- **Greenfield:** setup interview captures targets + active gates + tiers; steady-state `scope:complete` classifies + cost-stamps each item.
- **Brownfield:** run `task capacity:backfill` — confirm targets, skim low-confidence batch. Window-first; dry-run-default; git-reversible. Cost accrues forward only.

## Delivery (sliced, not big-bang)
1. **#987 intra-bucket ordering** (`plan.metadata.rank` + renderer / Phase 0) — smallest; + spec-readiness eligibility.
2. **Selection ordering** (continuation precedence + deficit-biased selection).
3. **Judgment gate engine** (`judgmentGates[]` + tiers + `verify:judgment-gates` + default-on universals + `gate_clearances[]`/`cleared_scope`).
4. **Capacity accounting** (`capacityAllocation` + kind-aware counting + flow enforcement + `minSampleSize` + `completedAt` + outcome overlay + cost capture/overlay (`capacity:cost-sync` via the Analytics API) + `capacity:show` + shared nudge-ranking + `task capacity:backfill`).
5. **Review & autonomy** (pending-human-decisions surface; autonomy dial; gate-tier composition with review-cycle).
6. **Lifecycle hygiene** (epic staleness + stranded-slice nudge + trichotomy).
7. **Enforcement + #1387 integration** (block modes, headless clearance gating, audit log, block-gated-solo).

## Deferred to v2 (do not lose)
1. **`weighted` capacity unit** (size→weight). *Stopgap:* `vbrief-count` + `estimatedChildren`.
2. **`cost` capacity unit** (credit/$ denominator). *Stopgap:* cost reporting overlay + `plan.metadata.cost` capture (Analytics API). *Trigger:* enough captured actuals + spend skew that count-mode masks.
3. **Per-commit `vBRIEF:`-trailer attribution for batched block-gated stories.** *Stopgap:* block-gated ship solo.
4. **Secret-content scanner** (key-shaped-string detection). *Stopgap:* path globs + `body-text` + PR-time diff check.
5. **Split `cognitive-debt` into its own bucket.** *Stopgap:* folded into `agentic-debt`. *Trigger:* a **context/doc drift** signal becomes available.
6. **Advisory heuristic annotation for untagged `declared` gates.** *Stopgap:* agent-assisted tagging at grooming.

## Migration & Compatibility
Existing vBRIEF trees remain valid; all new fields default to absent → today's behavior. Brownfield projects use `task capacity:backfill`. Cost actuals accrue forward only.

## Decisions Log
- **OQ1 — default `match` globs:** "both, layered."
- **OQ2 — `weighted` capacity:** deferred to v2 (`vbrief-count` + `estimatedChildren`).
- **OQ3 — `declared`-gate PR-time check:** honor tier for detectable/tagged; annotate-only for untagged; optional `paths` backstop.
- **OQ4 — `defaultEpicEstimate` + staleness:** default 3; absent → immediate nudge; `epicStalenessDays` default 14.
- **Clearance staleness:** binds to `cleared_scope`; scope creep re-triggers.
- **Re-bucketing:** in-flight allowed, frozen at completion.
- **Gate-blocked = reserved capacity:** counts toward bucket; `blocked` sub-count surfaced.
- **Multi-vBRIEF PR attribution:** `vBRIEF:` trailer + `file_scope` cross-check + fail-closed, pre-squash; v1 block-gated-solo.
- **Small-N balancing:** enforce over the completion flow; deficit-biased selection; `minSampleSize` guard. `wipCap` = concurrency, buckets = longitudinal mix.
- **Running totals:** derived; no stored total; optional rebuildable cache.
- **Effort vs value:** capacity measures effort; separate **outcome overlay** (revert/rework) and **cost overlay** close the loop.
- **Stranded slices:** completed slice keeps its bucket; debt forward-recognized via `epicStrandedDays` + trichotomy.
- **Continuation precedence:** `urgent/blocking > continuation > net-new(deficit) > rank > date`; oldest-started first; cancel valve; optional `finishBeforeStart`.
- **Session-start nudge budgeting:** budget 1 + overflow; rate-of-harm tiers; aggregated; Tier-1 persists; shared ranking function.
- **Brownfield cold-start:** `minSampleSize` counts *classified* completions; `task capacity:backfill` one-time migration; window-first; dry-run-default; re-run safe no-op; `--force --confirm` never clobbers `human`.
- **Review model:** automated multi-LLM review is the default first pass; the scarce resource is **human-clearance throughput**, surfaced as a pending-decisions backlog and relieved by the autonomy dial.
- **Risk-tiered gates:** gates carry a `tier` (`auto`/`review`/`block`) + `requiredHumanReviewers`, not binary; composes with the autonomy dial.
- **Spec-readiness eligibility:** only swarm-ready/well-specified work is promotable; reuse `swarm:readiness`.
- **Cost capture (rev 12 → rev 13):** start collecting actuals now via additive `plan.metadata.cost = { credits, tokens, usd, source, partial, asOf }` — **never agent self-report**. Primary source is the **Warp Enterprise Analytics API** `events` endpoint (per-message `credit_charged`, covering interactive + cloud), synced post-hoc by **`task capacity:cost-sync`** and attributed via `git_context.branch`/`head` + `conversation_id` (with the `vBRIEF:` trailer for batched sessions); harness OTEL / API `usage` fill `tokens` where available; `usd` derived via a credit→$ rate; `source`+`partial` provenance. Two-tier coverage: **enterprise-grounded** vs **estimate-only** (`deft-directive-cost`) below enterprise. **warpdotdev/warp#12075** narrowed to sub-enterprise access + raw token/$; cost-as-`unit` deferred.
- **Cognitive-debt drift:** context/doc drift is the measurable signal that could graduate cognitive debt to its own bucket.
- **Receipts:** durable committed audit (`xbrief/.audit/`) for authority-bearing events; gitignored `xbrief/.eval/` telemetry for selection traces.

## Open Questions v2 (research-informed)
- **Autonomy ratchet metric:** exact signal + thresholds for advancing/retreating the autonomy level.
- **Cost as a capacity `unit`** vs a permanent reporting overlay (depends on captured-actuals coverage; now grounded for enterprise via the Analytics API — credits, not tokens; sub-enterprise coverage pending warpdotdev/warp#12075).
- **Cognitive-debt graduation:** which drift metric is reliable enough to make it its own bucket.
- **LLM-reviewer disagreement routing:** policy for when conflicting/erroring multi-LLM reviews escalate to human adjudication (and how that interacts with gate tiers).

## References
- #987 (originating issue)
- `scripts/triage_classify.py` (match DSL + universal-rule layering)
- `scripts/policy.py`, `task policy:show` (typed-policy + audit-row pattern)
- `scripts/swarm_readiness.py` (`file_scope`/spec-readiness contract)
- `task migrate:vbrief` (one-time migration pattern reused by `capacity:backfill`)
- `deft-directive-review-cycle` (multi-LLM review), `deft-directive-cost` (pre-build estimate; calibrated by post-build actuals)
- Warp Enterprise Analytics API — https://docs.warp.dev/enterprise/enterprise-features/analytics-api/ (`summary`/`users`/`events`; per-message `credit_charged` + `git_context`; enterprise/admin-only; primary cost-capture source)
- Upstream: **warpdotdev/warp#12075** (narrowed to sub-enterprise access + raw token/$ exposure; enterprise interactive+cloud capture now unblocked via the Analytics API)
- AGENTS.md: pre-`start_agent` gate stack (#1378), headless launch (#1387), template propagation (#1309), SCM boundary (#1145), filesystem-truth in-flight count (#1270), swarm per-story checkpoint commits, session-start ritual + D2 suppression (#1149 / #1143)

- Industry best-practice basis: Anthropic 2026 Agentic Coding Trends Report; 2025 DORA findings; CodeScene (code-health/coverage signals); autonomy-dial + risk-tiered-escalation patterns; multi-agent production post-mortems (cost caps, cascade/blast-radius, receipts-not-chat-logs).

### 2026-06-05-1001-fixrelease-publish-rest-releasestagstag-404s-on-draft-releas: fix(release_publish): REST `/releases/tags/{tag}` 404s on draft releases (post-#961 regression)  `[completed]`

## Problem

During the v0.26.2 release on 2026-05-08, `task release:publish -- 0.26.2` failed with:

```
[publish] View v0.26.2 on deftai/directive... FAIL (release v0.26.2 not found on deftai/directive: gh: Not Found (HTTP 404))
```

This blocked the canonical Phase 6 publish branch in `skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md`.

## Root cause

`scripts/release_publish.py` was migrated to REST in #961 to route around the GraphQL bucket. The REST `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/tags/{tag}` endpoint **only finds published releases** by tag — it returns 404 for drafts, even though the draft has a `tag_name` field.

GitHub's draft release URL format confirms this asymmetry: `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/tag/untagged-<hash>` (note the `untagged-` prefix on drafts vs `v<version>` on published).

The legacy `gh release view <tag>` CLI surface uses GraphQL and does find drafts. The REST migration in #961 inadvertently regressed this case.

## Reproduction

1. `task release -- <version>` → lands draft
2. Verify draft via `gh release view v<version>` (works — GraphQL)
3. `task release:publish -- <version>` → 404 (REST `/releases/tags/{tag}` doesn't find drafts)

## Workaround used during v0.26.2 cut

```
gh release edit v0.26.2 --repo deftai/directive --draft=false
```

Direct `gh release edit` is GraphQL-backed and works on drafts. This is the manual recovery the operator used when `release_publish.py` failed.

## Suggested fix

Three options (ordered by preference):

1. **Fetch by ID, not by tag.** `release_publish.py` already calls `gh release view` (or could) to get the release ID, then PATCH `/releases/{id}` with `draft=false`. The by-ID REST endpoint works for both drafts and published releases.
2. **List all releases and match `tag_name`.** `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases` returns drafts in the list; iterate to find the matching `tag_name`. Slower (paginated) but works.
3. **Document the gap** and route this specific call through `gh release edit --draft=false` (GraphQL) as a documented exception, similar to the `gh pr ready` and `gh pr review --approve` exceptions already documented in `scripts/gh_rest.py` module docstring.

Option 1 is the cleanest. Option 3 is the smallest patch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `task release:publish -- <version>` succeeds against a draft release without falling back to manual `gh release edit`.
- [ ] AC-2: New regression test in `tests/cli/test_release_publish.py` covering the draft-tag-lookup case (REST 404 -> draft-aware fallback).
- [ ] AC-3: `scripts/gh_rest.py` module docstring updated if option 3 is taken (route documentation).
