### 2026-06-05-1002-fixtriage-bootstrap-cp1252-decode-unicodedecodeerror-in-subp: fix(triage_bootstrap): cp1252 decode UnicodeDecodeError in subprocess._readerthread on Windows (#798 chain at new surface)  `[completed]`

## Problem

During the 2026-05-08 v0.26.2 swarm session, an early measurement run of `pytest tests/test_triage_bootstrap.py tests/integration/test_triage_bootstrap_at_scale.py --durations=20` surfaced a `PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning` from `subprocess._readerthread`:

```
UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x8f in position 7610: character maps to <undefined>
  File "C:\Users\msadams\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\Lib\subprocess.py", line 1599, in _readerthread
    buffer.append(fh.read())
  File "C:\Users\msadams\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\Lib\encodings\cp1252.py", line 23, in decode
```

The failure originated in `tests/test_triage_bootstrap.py::test_populate_cache_defers_when_cache_module_missing`. The test passed (warning, not failure) but the underlying bug is real: `triage_bootstrap` shells out to a subprocess whose stdout contains non-ASCII content; the subprocess reader thread decodes via the active Windows codepage (cp1252) instead of UTF-8.

## Root cause

This is the **#798 chain at a new surface**. Per AGENTS.md `## PowerShell` section: "On Windows PowerShell 5.1, ANY modification of a file containing non-ASCII content MUST go through Python `pathlib.Path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` / `write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")`." The same root cause applies to subprocess piping: when Python's `subprocess.run` / `subprocess.Popen` is called without `encoding="utf-8"`, `_readerthread` decodes via the OS default codepage on Windows (cp1252) and corrupts/raises on multi-byte UTF-8 bytes.

The `scripts/triage_bootstrap.py::_infer_repo_from_git` already passes `timeout=10` (post-#952) but does NOT pass `encoding="utf-8"`. Other subprocess seams in the same module likely have the same gap.

The scanner gate `scripts/verify_encoding.py` (#798 deterministic-tier) checks tracked text files but cannot see runtime subprocess decode failures.

## Reproduction

```
cd C:\Repos\deft\directive
uv run pytest tests/test_triage_bootstrap.py tests/integration/test_triage_bootstrap_at_scale.py --durations=20 -q
```

Observe `PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning` in the warnings summary.

## Suggested fix

Grep `scripts/triage_bootstrap.py` (and any sibling `_triage_bootstrap_*.py` modules) for `subprocess.run(` / `subprocess.Popen(` / `subprocess.check_output(` calls. For every call:

1. Add `encoding="utf-8"` (or `text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"`)
2. If the call uses `capture_output=True`, ensure the decode of `result.stdout` / `result.stderr` is also UTF-8

Minimum AC:
- AC-1: All `subprocess.*` calls in `scripts/triage_bootstrap.py` and `scripts/_triage_bootstrap_*.py` pass `encoding="utf-8"` (or equivalent).
- AC-2: New regression test in `tests/test_triage_bootstrap.py` that injects non-ASCII output into a fake subprocess and verifies the parent decodes cleanly without `UnicodeDecodeError`.
- AC-3: `pytest tests/test_triage_bootstrap.py --durations=20 -W error::UserWarning` no longer surfaces `PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning`.
- AC-4: Audit other `scripts/` files for the same pattern (`subprocess.*` without `encoding=`) and either fix in this PR or file follow-up issues per call site.
- AC-5: CHANGELOG entry under `[Unreleased]` / `### Fixed`.
- AC-6: `meta/lessons.md` cross-reference under the existing `## PS 5.1 Non-ASCII Round-Trip Corruption -- elevated to deterministic tier (2026-05)` section noting this is a runtime-subprocess variant of the same chain.

## Recurrence record

#798 chain (read-side codepage decode):
- #236 (t1.11.1, scm/github.md prose tier)
- #240 (t1.11.2, multi-line here-string rule)
- #283 (t1.20.1, AGENTS.md UTF8Encoding rule)
- PR #795 (2026-05-01, 132-line CHANGELOG mojibake)
- #798 (2026-05-01, deterministic-tier elevation via `scripts/verify_encoding.py`)
- **THIS ISSUE** (2026-05-08, runtime-subprocess variant in `triage_bootstrap`)

The deterministic gate elevated the **file-write** side. The **subprocess-read** side is still prose tier and reproduces here.

## Related

- #798 -- file-write deterministic gate (the existing rule covers static text files; subprocess decode is runtime)
- #952 -- `triage_bootstrap` watchdog timeout (most recent change to the affected module; the cp1252 surface predates it)
- #951 -- `task triage:bootstrap` flag scrub
- AGENTS.md `## PowerShell` section
- `meta/lessons.md` `## PS 5.1 Non-ASCII Round-Trip Corruption` section

## Out of scope

- Auditing every `scripts/*.py` subprocess seam in this PR; AC-4 just flags the audit, follow-up issues per file are acceptable
- Elevating subprocess-decode to deterministic-tier (would require a new gate beyond `verify_encoding.py`); deferred to a follow-up if recurrence continues

**Acceptance**:

- All triage_bootstrap subprocess reads decode stdout as UTF-8. `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given non-ASCII bytes on a subprocess stdout, when triage_bootstrap reads the output, then every subprocess call decodes it as UTF-8 without raising UnicodeDecodeError.
- The triage_bootstrap suite no longer emits the cp1252 reader-thread warning. `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: When the triage:bootstrap test suite runs with the unhandled-thread-exception warning escalated, then no cp1252 charmap decode warning is emitted from the reader thread.
- Regression test covers the cp1252 reader-thread decode path. `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: A regression test in tests/test_triage_bootstrap.py injects high-byte output into a fake subprocess and validates that the parent decodes the stream cleanly.
- lessons.md records the runtime-subprocess variant of the #798 chain. `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: When meta/lessons.md is read, then it records the runtime-subprocess cp1252 variant cross-referenced to the existing #798 deterministic-tier section.

### 2026-06-05-1003-fixscriptsresolve-changelog-unreleased-dedup-gap-on-truncate: fix(scripts/resolve_changelog_unreleased): dedup gap on truncated/issue-numberless entries (#911 follow-up)  `[completed]`

## Problem

The `task changelog:resolve-unreleased` helper (shipped in v0.26.2 from #911) was dogfooded across the v0.26.2 cohort cascade (5 PRs, 4 sequential rebases). The helper resolved every CHANGELOG conflict cleanly, BUT the published `CHANGELOG.md` for v0.26.2 contains **two truncated `gh_rest.py` header lines** (lines 26 and 28 of the released file) that are partial duplicates of the full entry on line 30:

```markdown
- **feat(scripts): `gh_rest.py` REST-fallback helpers
- **perf(tests,tasks): mark watchdog tests slow ... (#975)** -- ...
- **feat(scripts): `gh_rest.py` REST-fallback helpers
- **feat(scripts,tasks,skills): CHANGELOG union-merge helper for swarm cascade conflicts (#911)** -- ...
- **feat(scripts): `gh_rest.py` REST-fallback helpers for `gh` mutations and reads (#961)** -- ...
```

The truncated stubs are orphan headers (entry-start `- **` with no closing `**`, no body, no `(#NNN)` issue number) that the helper preserved as if they were distinct entries.

## Root cause

The helper's dedup heuristic (per `scripts/resolve_changelog_unreleased.py`) is:

> Keep all HEAD entries; for each branch entry, if not present in HEAD by `(#NNN)` issue-number heuristic, prepend it under its subsection.

The heuristic matches by parenthesized issue numbers. When an entry is **truncated** mid-line and lacks a closing `**` and a `(#NNN)` reference, the helper has no key to dedup on — it treats the stub as a unique entry and prepends it on the next rebase. The cascading rebases in the v0.26.2 release (4 sequential rebases of agent5 → agent2 → agent4 → agent3 onto master) compounded this: each rebase introduced a new truncated stub of the upstream `gh_rest.py` header, and the helper preserved each as distinct.

Likely upstream cause: an earlier branch resolved a CHANGELOG conflict via a different path (manual `edit_files` or pre-helper splice) that produced the first truncated stub. Once a truncated stub exists in master, every subsequent rebase reproduces it because the helper cannot collapse it with the full entry.

## Reproduction

The v0.26.2 published `CHANGELOG.md` is the recurrence record. To reproduce synthetically:

1. Construct a CHANGELOG with `[Unreleased]/### Added` containing a full entry `- **feat(scripts): \`gh_rest.py\` REST-fallback helpers for \`gh\` mutations and reads (#961)** -- <body>`.
2. Inject a truncated orphan header above it: `- **feat(scripts): \`gh_rest.py\` REST-fallback helpers` (no closing `**`, no `(#NNN)`).
3. Add a conflict block with branch-side adding ANOTHER orphan stub.
4. Run `task changelog:resolve-unreleased` -- the orphan stub is preserved instead of collapsed.

Unit-test surface: `tests/cli/test_resolve_changelog_unreleased.py` adds a fixture with the orphan-stub shape and asserts post-resolve content has at most one occurrence of the header prefix.

## Impact

- **Cosmetic now** (v0.26.2 already published with the duplicates).
- **Recurring** — the helper will keep producing these on every future cascade until fixed. The bug compounds: 4 rebases produced 2 stubs; an 8-rebase cascade would produce 4+.
- **Not a load-bearing data loss** — the full entry on line 30 has the canonical content; the orphan stubs are visual noise, not lost commits.

## Suggested fix

Three options (ordered by preference):

1. **Detect orphan-header lines in `parse_side`** -- treat any entry-start (`- **` or `* **`) that lacks a closing `**` on the same line as a malformed entry. Either (a) attach the malformed line to the next valid entry as continuation, or (b) refuse to dedup against valid entries (so a manual edit_files fallback is the resolution). Option (b) is the smaller patch.

2. **Content-based dedup fallback** -- when an entry has no `(#NNN)`, fall back to a content-prefix match against existing HEAD entries. Compute a normalized prefix (e.g. first 60 chars of the entry text) and skip the branch entry if any HEAD entry has the same prefix.

3. **Refuse-on-orphan, exit 1 "unresolvable"** -- detect malformed entries and exit 1 with a diagnostic pointing at line numbers, forcing manual `edit_files`. Safest but loses the auto-resolve property.

Recommend option 1(b) + option 2 layered: malformed entries don't dedup against valid ones, AND content-prefix match catches the orphan-stub case before it propagates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `scripts/resolve_changelog_unreleased.py` detects orphan-header lines (entry-start without closing `**` AND without `(#NNN)`) and either attaches to next valid entry OR drops them with a stderr WARN.
- [ ] AC-2: Content-prefix dedup fallback for entries without `(#NNN)` references.
- [ ] AC-3: New regression tests in `tests/cli/test_resolve_changelog_unreleased.py` covering: (a) orphan-stub on HEAD side, (b) orphan-stub on branch side, (c) orphan-stub on both sides matching same content, (d) cascading rebase synthetic that produces multiple orphan stubs and verifies they collapse into one.
- [ ] AC-4: Run the new test suite against the v0.26.2 published CHANGELOG as a fixture; assert the helper would have collapsed the line-26/28 stubs.
- [ ] AC-5: Optional follow-up commit on master that cleans up the v0.26.2 line-26/28 stubs in the existing `[0.26.2]` section. NOT a release-tag amend (the dist zip is published); just a chore commit on master so the next release's `[Unreleased]` slate inherits a clean prior section.
- [ ] AC-6: CHANGELOG entry under `[Unreleased]` / `### Fixed`.

## Recurrence record

First occurrence: v0.26.2 release on 2026-05-08, 5-PR cohort cascade with 4 sequential rebases produced 2 truncated `gh_rest.py` stubs in published CHANGELOG.md.

## Related

- #911 -- the helper that ships with this dedup gap (the bug ships in the same release as the helper itself, ironically validated by the helper's own dogfood)
- #999 -- PR that landed #911
- #961 -- the `gh_rest.py` entry that the orphan stubs partially duplicate
- The 2026-05-04 v0.25.1 cascade is the original recurrence record that motivated #911 (HEAD-take dropped entries); the new bug is a different failure mode of the union-merge fix

## Out of scope

- Refactoring the helper's data model from line-based parsing to AST-style tokenization; the prefix-match heuristic is sufficient for the v1 patch
- Releasing a v0.26.3 just for this fix; queue under `[Unreleased]` for the next batch

**Acceptance**:

- Truncated orphan headers do not dedup against valid entries. `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given a truncated orphan header without a closing ** or a (#NNN) reference, when the helper resolves the section, then it refuses to dedup the stub against valid entries and drops it with a stderr warning.
- Content-prefix fallback dedups entries that lack an issue number. `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given an entry with no (#NNN) reference, when the helper dedups, then a content-prefix match collapses it against an existing HEAD entry that shares the same prefix.
- Matching orphan stubs on both sides collapse to a single header. `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given orphan stubs on both the HEAD and branch sides matching the same content, when the helper resolves, then the output retains at most one occurrence of the header prefix.
- Regression test replays a cascading-rebase synthetic. `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: A regression test in tests/cli/test_resolve_changelog_unreleased.py replays a cascading-rebase synthetic and validates that multiple orphan stubs collapse into a single entry.

### 2026-06-05-1027-coverage-threshold-blind-spot-pygametkinter-event-loops-cant: Coverage threshold blind spot: pygame/tkinter event loops can't run headlessly, dragging overall % below 85% threshold  `[completed]`

## Summary
The deft 85% coverage threshold assumption fails for projects where the primary source file contains pygame/tkinter/Electron event loops that cannot execute without a display. This causes a silent false-pass during agent implementation (agent reports high coverage) followed by a check failure when the full src/ is measured.

## Observed impact
During a desktop-UI swarm agent run:
- Agent reported 97% coverage (measured only files it had imported in its test session)
- After the fix commit, full 	ask check showed 69% — src/ui.py at 43% dragged the total below threshold
- Required adding src/ui.py to [tool.coverage.run] omit in pyproject.toml as a workaround

The 85% threshold is correct for logic-heavy code but creates friction for any project whose project_type is Desktop App or TUI.

## Proposed fix
One or more of:
1. The deft-directive-setup Phase 2 output for project_type = Desktop App should scaffold pyproject.toml with a coverage.run.omit entry for src/ui.py (or equivalent display-dependent entry point)
2. The Python language file (languages/python.md) should document the headless-test pattern: os.environ.setdefault("SDL_VIDEODRIVER", "dummy") and coverage omit for event-loop modules
3. The setup skill should warn when project_type = Desktop App: "pygame/tkinter event loops cannot be tested headlessly — consider excluding UI entry points from coverage measurement"

## Source
Discovered during tic-tac-toe desktop-UI swarm agent (2026-05-10). pyproject.toml patched mid-session.

**Acceptance**:

- Setup skill warns about headless coverage for Desktop App projects. `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given project_type is Desktop App, when the setup skill runs Phase 2, then it emits a warning that pygame/tkinter event loops cannot be tested headlessly and suggests a coverage omit for the UI entry point.
- python.md records the headless-test pattern and a coverage omit example. `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: When languages/python.md is read, then it records the SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy headless-test pattern and a coverage.run omit example for event-loop modules.
- Applying the omit lets task check pass on a desktop-UI project. `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given a desktop-UI project, when the recommended coverage omit is applied, then task check measures only logic modules and no longer fails on the display-dependent entry point.

### 2026-06-05-1525-fixinstall-adopt-codeql-recognized-zip-slip-barrier-in-extra: fix(install): adopt CodeQL-recognized zip-slip barrier in extractCoreTarball (clears go/zipslip alert #6)  `[completed]`

## Summary

CodeQL code-scanning alert #6 (`go/zipslip`, security severity HIGH) flags `extractCoreTarball` in `cmd/deft-install/upgrade.go` even though the extractor is already guarded against path traversal. The finding is a **false positive caused by an unrecognized sanitizer shape**, not a real vulnerability — but we want a green scan rather than a standing dismissal.

## Why CodeQL still flags it

The current guards are correct but not the form CodeQL's `go/zipslip` model recognizes:
- Traversal is rejected with a per-segment loop (`seg == ".."`), not `strings.Contains(name, "..")`.
- The containment barrier checks `filepath.Clean(target)`, while the `os.MkdirAll` / `os.OpenFile` sinks consume the raw `target` value — so CodeQL does not propagate the barrier to the sink.

CodeQL's documented "GOOD" sanitizer (rule help for `go/zipslip`) is `strings.Contains(name, "..")` on the entry name, dominating the filesystem sinks.

## Fix

In `extractCoreTarball`, replace the per-segment `..` loop with the CodeQL-recognized barrier on the raw entry name:

```go
if strings.Contains(name, "..") {
    return "", fmt.Errorf("tar entry contains a '..' path element: %q", hdr.Name)
}
```

Keep the existing `HasPrefix(filepath.Clean(target), dest+sep)` check and symlink-skip as defense-in-depth. Add a regression test that a `..`-containing tar entry is rejected and nothing escapes the destination.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-1: `extractCoreTarball` rejects any tar entry whose name contains `..`, with a regression test in `cmd/deft-install/upgrade_test.go`.
- AC-2: existing extractor tests still pass; `task check` green.
- AC-3: after merge, CodeQL re-scan resolves `go/zipslip` alert #6 (or, if it persists, dismiss as confirmed false positive).
- AC-4: CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry.

## Notes

The input is a trusted GitHub source tarball (`codeload` for `deftai/directive`), so real-world exploitability was already near-zero; this change is to satisfy the scanner's recognized-barrier shape. Refs code-scanning alert #6.

**Acceptance**:

- AC-1:  rejects any tar entry whose name contains , with a regression test in . `[proposed]`
- AC-2: existing extractor tests still pass;  green. `[proposed]`
- AC-3: after merge, CodeQL re-scan resolves  alert #6 (or, if it persists, dismiss as confirmed false positive). `[proposed]`
- AC-4: CHANGELOG  entry. `[proposed]`

### 2026-06-05-1528-fixinstall-strengthen-zip-slip-barrier-at-source-sink-to-cle: fix(install): strengthen zip-slip barrier at source + sink to clear go/zipslip alert #6 (follow-up to #1525)  `[completed]`

## Summary

Follow-up to #1525 / PR #1526. That change adopted `strings.Contains(name, "..")` (on the derived `name`) to clear CodeQL `go/zipslip` alert #6, but the post-merge `master` CodeQL re-scan still reports the alert OPEN at `cmd/deft-install/upgrade.go:414` — verified via the code-scanning instances API (`refs/heads/master 5b4b680 state=open`). The PR-ref check that suggested "cleared" was misleading: CodeQL PR analysis does not re-list a pre-existing alert per PR ref, so the authoritative signal is the default-branch re-scan, which still flags it.

## Why the first attempt missed

- The barrier checked the *derived* `name`, not the original taint source `hdr.Name` (the value CodeQL tracks from `tr.Next()` at line 414).
- The containment check validated `filepath.Clean(target)` while the `os.MkdirAll` / `os.OpenFile` sinks consumed the raw `target` — so CodeQL's dataflow never saw the validated value reach the sink.

## Fix (iteration 2)

1. Sanitize the **raw `hdr.Name`** at the source: `if strings.Contains(hdr.Name, "..") { return error }` immediately after the header read, before any path derivation.
2. Validate the **exact `target`** that flows to the sinks: `filepath.Join` already returns a cleaned path, so check `strings.HasPrefix(target, cleanDest+sep)` on `target` itself (drop the separate `filepath.Clean(target)` copy).
3. Remove the now-redundant `name`-based barrier.

The existing `TestExtractCoreTarball_RejectsPathTraversal` still covers rejection.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-1: barrier sanitizes `hdr.Name` at the source; sink consumes the validated `target`.
- AC-2: `task check` green; extractor tests pass.
- AC-3: after merge, the `master` CodeQL re-scan resolves `go/zipslip` alert #6 to "fixed". If it STILL persists despite this, dismiss alert #6 as a confirmed false positive (the extractor is provably safe).
- AC-4: CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry.

Refs #1525, code-scanning alert #6.

**Acceptance**:

- AC-1: barrier sanitizes  at the source; sink consumes the validated . `[proposed]`
- AC-2:  green; extractor tests pass. `[proposed]`
- AC-3: after merge, the  CodeQL re-scan resolves  alert #6 to "fixed". If it STILL persists despite this, dismiss alert #6 as a confirmed false positive (the extractor is provably safe). `[proposed]`
- AC-4: CHANGELOG  entry. `[proposed]`

### 2026-06-08-1531-swarm-opt-in-tiered-heterogeneous-dispatch-strong-model-orch: swarm: opt-in tiered / heterogeneous dispatch (strong-model orchestrator + cheap high-context leaf code-runners)  `[completed]`

## Summary

Make `deft-directive-swarm` support an **opt-in tiered / heterogeneous agent topology** across provider-neutral sub-agent backends, including Grok Build (`spawn_subagent`), Composer-class coding agents, Cursor/cloud agents, and future adapters: a strong-model **orchestrator/strategist** that spawns cheaper, high-context **leaf code-runners** (e.g. Composer-class models), each on one focused vBRIEF in an isolated worktree, with a strong-model **reviewer/merge** tier.

This is a provider-neutral extension of the existing platform adapter (#1342 / #1331), not a from-scratch capability. It maps directly to the two-agent (initializer + coding agent) and Layer 5 orchestrator -> Layer 7 commodity-coder architecture in `docs/the-harness-is-everything.md`.

## Scope update — provider-neutral sub-agent choice

This issue should not be limited to Grok Build routing. The user-facing capability is broader: when running coding work through `deft-directive-swarm` or related build/review flows, the operator should be able to choose which sub-agent backend handles leaf implementation work, including Composer-class agents, Grok Build agents, Cursor/cloud agents, or future coding-agent providers.

The design should separate three concerns:

1. **Dispatch provider** — the runtime primitive used to launch the child worker, such as `spawn_subagent`, Cursor Composer/task agents, cloud agents, or another adapter.
2. **Worker role** — what the child is allowed to do: leaf implementation, initializer/spec-tightening, review monitor, merge/rebase, or release gate.
3. **Model/agent selection** — the operator or harness policy that maps a role plus vBRIEF attributes to a concrete agent/model, for example Composer for code-runner work and a stronger model for orchestration/review.

This keeps Deft model-agnostic while still exposing enough structured metadata for the operator to route work intentionally. Grok Build remains one backend implementation of the idea, not the only target.

## Discussion needed — adapter shape

Before implementation, run a short design/discussion phase on the adapter contract. Open questions to resolve:

- Should Deft expose a first-class `subagentProvider` / `workerBackend` choice in policy, launch manifests, or swarm prompts, or should that remain external harness configuration?
- Should the choice be per cohort, per story, per role, or all three?
- What stable provider-neutral fields should every dispatch envelope carry so Composer, Grok Build, Cursor agents, and future tools can all route consistently?
- Which roles are safe for lower-cost coding agents, and which must stay on a strong/review-capable agent by policy?
- How should Deft record the selected backend in audit output so review cycles and postmortems know which worker type produced a change?

## Motivation

- **Cost / latency**: keep the expensive strategist turns rare; push the high-volume implementation work to cheap, fast, 200K-context leaf models.
- **Quality is gate-bounded, not model-bounded**: the skill's gates (`task check`, file-overlap audit, Greptile review cycle) are model-agnostic, so a weaker leaf model is acceptable for *implementation* as long as the gates hold and the spec is tight.

## Findings from design discussion

1. **deft treats `spawn_subagent` as an opaque dispatch primitive.** Every usage (Phase 3 Step 2d, preamble §9, `swarm/swarm.md`) passes only: canonical preamble + adapted worktree prompt + worktree path. There is no model / agent-type parameter anywhere on the deft side today.
2. **Model selection is a property of the GROKbuild harness — confirmed.** The operator configures a GROKbuild **routing file** that maps task attributes -> model (e.g. -> Composer 2.5). So deft neither pins nor needs to pin the child model; the router decides at the harness layer. This is the cleaner split: deft stays model-agnostic; GROKbuild routes.
   - **Design consequence**: the previously-proposed optional `worker_model` pass-through field on the dispatch token is likely **unnecessary**. deft's real leverage is making task attributes **legible to the router**, not selecting the model itself.
3. **Opt-in only.** Tiering is enabled by the operator's presence of a routing file; deft does not force it. A future `plan.policy.swarmTiering` setting could declare a repo's intended task-attribute -> tier mapping for documentation/consistency. No change to the default grok-build path otherwise.
4. **Model-tiering and the "initializer/document-writer" role ship together — they are one feature.** A cheap leaf model fails hardest on an under-specified vBRIEF, so the spec-tightening step is the *safety margin* for the cheap tier, not a follow-up. In deft this does NOT require a new heavyweight agent type: `deft-directive-decompose`, `task swarm:readiness`, and `deft-directive-refinement` already do the initializer's job. Express it as a pre-dispatch readiness gate.
5. **Routing is invisible to deft at dispatch time.** Because the GROKbuild routing file resolves the model after deft hands off, the swarm monitor cannot know which tier a given task will land on. Two consequences: (a) the spec-quality gate must be **unconditional** (applied to every swarm dispatch, not gated on a known-cheap tier); (b) deft must surface the routing signals so the router can classify reliably.

## Proposed scope (skill changes)

- **Phase 3 — Tiered / heterogeneous dispatch subsection**: document the topology (strategist/orchestrator, initializer/doc-writer, code-runner) and the routing-file-driven model assignment, with the safety rule that **gates, review cycle, merge cascade, and conflict-resolution rebase stay on the strong model**; only leaf *implementation* is routed to the cheap tier.
- **Expose routing signals**: ensure the vBRIEF / dispatch envelope surfaces the attributes the GROKbuild routing file keys on (candidate signals: `plan.metadata.kind`, labels, acceptance-criteria count / complexity, file scope) so the router can classify tasks deterministically. deft stays model-agnostic.
- **Unconditional pre-dispatch readiness gate**: every vBRIEF dispatched into the swarm MUST pass `task swarm:readiness` clean and have non-empty, file-scoped `plan.items` — because deft cannot see which model the router will assign, the tight-spec safety margin applies to all dispatches.
- **Phase 4**: make the heartbeat sweep (#1365) explicitly recursive for trees of depth > 1.

## Risks / guardrails

- Never route the cheap model onto the merge cascade, Phase 5->6 release gate, or conflict-resolution rebase (irreversible-damage surfaces) — keep those task attributes mapped to the strong tier in the routing file.
- The Duplicate-Agent failure mode multiplies with tree depth — heartbeats required at every level.
- Keep the orchestrator conversation shallow (existing Phase 4 context-length discipline).

## Open questions

1. **What does the GROKbuild routing file key on?** (task type, labels, file globs, explicit tag, heuristic?) — determines which signals deft must make legible in the vBRIEF / dispatch envelope. _(Routing file now exists; need its keys to align deft's exposed attributes.)_
2. Should deft document a `plan.policy.swarmTiering` mapping that mirrors the routing file, or leave tiering entirely operator-owned in GROKbuild?
3. How does deft keep its exposed signals in sync with the routing file so they don't drift?

## References

- `skills/deft-directive-swarm/SKILL.md` (Phase 3 Step 2d, Phase 4)
- `templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md` §9 (sub-agent spawn rules), #1378 (`## Allocation context` token)
- `docs/the-harness-is-everything.md` (initializer + coding agent; orchestrator/commodity-coder layering)
- #1342 (platform adapter / spawn_subagent launch path), #1331 (runtime decoupling), #1365 (heartbeat contract)

---

_Filed from a design discussion; to be iterated._

**Acceptance**:

- Document provider-neutral sub-agent backend selection in the swarm skill `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given the swarm skill is read by an operator, when it describes tiered or heterogeneous dispatch, then it explicitly separates dispatch provider, worker role, and model or agent selection instead of presenting Grok Build as the only supported backend.
- Define safe role boundaries for cheaper coding agents `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given a user wants to route leaf coding work to Composer or another cheaper coding agent, the guidance states that orchestration, review-cycle decisions, conflict-resolution rebase, merge, and release gates remain mapped to strong/review-capable agents.
- Add tests that pin provider-neutral swarm guidance `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given the content test suite runs, it fails if the swarm guidance omits Composer-class agents or future adapters, or if it regresses to a Grok Build-only description of sub-agent routing.

### 2026-06-08-1538-linux-installer-yes-reports-missing-core-tools-instead-of-bo: Linux installer --yes reports missing core tools instead of bootstrapping them  `[completed]`

## Summary
The published Linux installer succeeds in WSL, but in `--yes` mode it does not install/bootstrap the core follow-up tools it detects as missing. It reports `uv`, `task`, and `gh` as missing, with doctor also warning on `go` and `node`.

## Repro
Environment: fresh WSL2 Ubuntu, default user `msadams`.

Commands:

```bash
curl -L -o /home/msadams/install-linux-amd64 https://github.com/deftai/directive/releases/latest/download/install-linux-amd64
chmod +x /home/msadams/install-linux-amd64
rm -rf /home/msadams/repos/deft/installer-smoke
mkdir -p /home/msadams/repos/deft/installer-smoke
/home/msadams/install-linux-amd64 --yes --repo-root /home/msadams/repos/deft/installer-smoke --json
```

Observed installer version:

```text
deft-install v0.42.1
```

## Observed
The install itself exits 0 and deposits `.deft/core`, `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/skills`, `.githooks`, `Taskfile.yml`, `xbrief/`, and guard files correctly. However, output includes:

```text
Missing core tools (consent implied by --yes): gh, task, uv
  Fallbacks (run manually or via platform package manager):
    Windows: winget install --id <ID> or scripts/setup_windows.ps1
    macOS:   brew install go-task uv python gh
    Linux:   apt/brew equivalent for task uv python3 gh
```

The doctor handoff then reports:

```json
{"check":"dependency","message":"uv (Astral Python runner) not found - required - install: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/","severity":"error","tool":"uv"}
```

and warnings for `task`, `go`, and `node`.

## Expected
In Linux `--yes` / non-interactive mode, the installer should either:

1. bootstrap required core tools where safe/portable, at least `uv`, `task`, and `gh`; or
2. fail loud before claiming install success if required post-install doctor dependencies cannot be satisfied automatically; or
3. clearly document that Linux tool bootstrap is not implemented and that `--yes` only reports missing tools.

The current message says consent is implied by `--yes`, which suggests the installer should take action rather than only emit fallback instructions.

## Notes
This came from setting up a fresh WSL maintainer lane to verify the Linux installer path. The installer payload deposit worked; the issue is the expected core-tool bootstrap behavior after detection.

**Acceptance**:

- Bootstrap or fail-loud for missing Linux core tools in non-interactive installer runs `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given a fresh Linux or WSL environment missing uv, task, and gh, when install-linux-amd64 --yes --repo-root <project> --json runs and the supported bootstrap path is available, then the installer installs or wires those required tools and the JSON result does not leave them in missing_tools.
- Report unsupported Linux bootstrap as a deterministic installer failure `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given a Linux environment where the installer cannot safely bootstrap required tools, when the non-interactive install reaches the core-tool phase, then it exits non-zero with structured actionable output instead of printing consent implied by --yes and still claiming install success.
- Add focused installer tests for the Linux missing-tool branch `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given mocked tool discovery and bootstrap outcomes, the installer test suite asserts the success, failure, and fallback-output behavior for Linux --yes missing-tool handling without requiring real apt, brew, network access, or root privileges.

### 2026-06-08-1543-review-cycle-handle-greptile-informal-clean-replies-without: review-cycle: handle Greptile informal clean replies without canonical fields  `[completed]`

## Summary
PR #1541 exposed a review-cycle gap: Greptile can post an informal clean reply that says the diff is clean, while omitting the canonical rolling-summary fields that Directive's merge gates require: `Last reviewed commit:` and `Confidence Score: X/5`.

The deterministic gates are correct to block in this state because they cannot prove the review is current or confidence is above the threshold. However, the review-cycle skill, poller prompt, and merge-readiness diagnostics should recognize this specific state and route it cleanly instead of leaving the swarm monitor in an ambiguous stall.

## Observed
- `task pr:merge-ready -- 1541` reports P0=0 and P1=0 but fails because it cannot parse `Last reviewed commit:` or `Confidence Score` from the Greptile body.
- `task swarm:verify-review-clean -- 1540 1541` blocks the cohort for the same reason.
- The latest Greptile bot comment on PR #1541 is human-readable and clean, but not the canonical rolling-summary format.

## Expected
Directive should fail loud with a targeted recovery path when Greptile posts an informal clean response without canonical fields.

The fix should not loosen the merge gate to accept prose such as "looks solid". It should preserve the requirement for current reviewed SHA and confidence evidence, or require an explicit documented override.

## Proposed scope
- Update `skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md` to document the "informal clean but missing canonical fields" state and the operator choices.
- Update `templates/swarm-greptile-poller-prompt.md` so pollers report this as a distinct terminal/blocked state instead of generic timeout/stall.
- Update `scripts/pr_merge_readiness.py` diagnostics to distinguish informal-clean missing fields from a review that is still writing or absent.
- Add focused tests for the parser/diagnostics and content guidance.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a Greptile bot comment that says prior issues are resolved / current diff is clean but omits `Last reviewed commit:` and `Confidence Score`, `task pr:merge-ready` exits non-zero with a diagnostic that names the informal-clean missing-canonical-fields state and gives a recovery path.
- Given a swarm cohort hits this state, the review-cycle guidance routes to either requesting a canonical Greptile summary/retrigger or a documented override, not silent polling.
- The merge gate still refuses to treat informal clean prose alone as merge-ready.
- Tests pin the parser behavior and the review-cycle/poller guidance.

## References
- PR #1541: provider backend policy story blocked by missing canonical Greptile fields
- PR #1540/#1541 Wave 1 swarm verifier: `task swarm:verify-review-clean -- 1540 1541`
- Related gates: `scripts/pr_merge_readiness.py`, `scripts/swarm_verify_review_clean.py`

**Acceptance**:

- Given a Greptile bot comment says prior issues are resolved and the current diff is clean but omits canonical fields, task pr:merge-ready exits non-zero with an informal-clean missing-canonical-fields diagnostic and recovery path. `[completed]`
  - Acceptance: Given a Greptile bot comment says prior issues are resolved and the current diff is clean but omits `Last reviewed commit:` and `Confidence Score`, `task pr:merge-ready` exits non-zero with a diagnostic that names the informal-clean missing-canonical-fields state and gives a recovery path.
- Given a swarm cohort hits this state, review-cycle and poller guidance routes to requesting canonical evidence, retriggering, or a documented override instead of silent polling. `[completed]`
  - Acceptance: Given a swarm cohort hits this state, the review-cycle guidance routes to either requesting a canonical Greptile summary/retrigger or a documented override, not silent polling.

### 2026-06-08-1554-installer-add-maintainer-mode-to-avoid-consumer-file-project: installer: add maintainer mode to avoid consumer file projections in framework repo  `[completed]`

## Summary
When the published Linux installer is run against the directive framework repository itself, it treats the checkout like a consumer project and rewrites/deposits consumer-managed files. Maintainer checkouts need a first-class installer mode that bootstraps tools and payload checks without replacing maintainer-owned project files.

Observed during Ubuntu/WSL validation of `deft-install v0.43.0`:

```bash
/home/msadams/install-linux-amd64 --yes --upgrade --repo-root /home/msadams/repos/deft/directive --json
```

The Linux bootstrap fix worked: missing `gh`, `task`, and `uv` were installed successfully. But the installer also staged consumer-style changes in the framework repo, including:

- `AGENTS.md` managed-section header rewritten toward consumer-installed shape
- `.gitignore` additions for `.deft/core.bak-*`, `.deft/*.bak-*`, and `xbrief/*.lock`
- `.gitattributes` additions marking `.deft/core/**` as generated/vendored
- consumer support files such as `greptile.json`, CodeQL config, core guard workflow, and lifecycle `.gitkeep` files

For a maintainer checkout, `AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore`, and `.gitattributes` must remain the repository-maintainer versions from the checkout, not the consumer installer projections.

## Proposal
Add an explicit maintainer mode to `cmd/deft-install`, for example:

```bash
deft-install --yes --upgrade --maintainer --repo-root /path/to/directive --json
```

## Expected behavior
In `--maintainer` mode, the installer should:

- Still perform Linux core-tool bootstrap in `--yes` mode (`gh`, `task`, `uv`) and report missing unsupported tools clearly.
- Detect that `--repo-root` is the directive framework repository or accept the explicit `--maintainer` flag as authority.
- Preserve maintainer-owned files such as `AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `Taskfile.yml`, repo workflows, and repo-local policy files unless a maintainer-specific update path explicitly owns them.
- Avoid depositing consumer-only guard/config files into the maintainer repo unless they are already part of the repo source of truth.
- Emit JSON that records `maintainer_mode: true` and lists any skipped consumer projections.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a directive framework checkout and `--maintainer`, when the Linux installer runs with `--yes --upgrade --json`, then it bootstraps missing core tools but leaves `AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore`, and `.gitattributes` byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Given a consumer project and no `--maintainer`, existing consumer install behavior remains unchanged.
- Given `--maintainer` outside a directive framework checkout, the installer fails loud or emits an actionable warning rather than silently applying the wrong projection.
- Tests cover maintainer mode in `cmd/deft-install/setup_test.go` with fixture assertions for skipped consumer projections and unchanged maintainer files.

## Labels
Suggested: `installer`, `enhancement`, `source-of-truth`.

**Acceptance**:

- Add maintainer-mode installer behavior `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given a directive framework checkout, when `deft-install --yes --upgrade --maintainer --repo-root <checkout> --json` runs, then `git status --short` shows no installer-created changes to tracked maintainer-owned files.
- Preserve consumer installer behavior `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given a consumer project, when the installer runs without `--maintainer`, then the existing consumer projection files are still created or updated and the consumer install tests continue to pass.
- Report maintainer tooling status `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given maintainer mode, when JSON output is requested, then the response includes separate maintainer-tool status for `go`, `node`, and `ghx` without marking those tools required for consumer mode.
- Document maintainer and consumer setup flows `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given the install docs, when a maintainer reads setup guidance, then README links to CONTRIBUTING for framework setup and getting-started does not duplicate maintainer instructions.

### 2026-06-08-1555-tooling-make-github-markdown-body-posting-safe-from-shell-su: tooling: make GitHub Markdown body posting safe from shell substitution  `[completed]`

## Summary
Agents can corrupt GitHub issue/comment bodies when Markdown containing backticks is embedded inside double-quoted shell commands. In Bash, text like `` `ghx` `` is command substitution, so the shell executes the command and replaces the intended literal Markdown before `gh api` receives the payload.

This happened during WSL validation while adding a `ghx` requirement to #1554: the intended phrase "include `ghx`" was posted as "include Work seamlessly with GitHub from the command line" because the shell expanded the backticked `ghx` token.

## Problem
Directive currently tells agents to prefer task/gh surfaces, but it does not give a deterministic safe path for posting Markdown-rich issue comments, PR bodies, or issue bodies. This leaves agents to hand-roll shell quoting around Markdown, which is brittle for backticks, dollar signs, here-doc boundaries, and other shell metacharacters.

## Proposal
Add a canonical safe body-posting surface and guidance, for example:

- A task wrapper that accepts body text from stdin or a file and calls `gh api` with `shell=False` / safe subprocess handling.
- Documentation/rules that forbid inline Markdown bodies with backticks inside double-quoted shell commands.
- Examples for creating/editing GitHub issues and comments using JSON/stdin, single-quoted heredocs, or temporary body files.
- Read-back guidance: use live `gh` immediately after mutations, because `ghx` may return cached stale GET responses.

## Acceptance criteria
- Directive rules or SCM docs explicitly warn that Markdown backticks inside double-quoted shell commands trigger shell command substitution.
- A canonical helper/task exists for posting GitHub issue/comment/PR Markdown bodies without shell interpolation.
- The helper uses safe subprocess capture (`encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"`) and avoids `shell=True`.
- Examples cover issue creation, issue comment creation, and issue comment edit/read-back.
- Tests cover a body containing literal backticks, dollar signs, quotes, and a fenced code block.

Refs #1554.

**Acceptance**:

- Add safe GitHub body posting helper `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given a Markdown body containing literal backticks, when the canonical helper posts it to a GitHub issue comment, then the live read-back contains the same backtick text unchanged.
- Document shell-substitution hazards and safe examples `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given the SCM and agent guidance, when an agent needs to post GitHub Markdown, then the docs show safe create, edit, and read-back examples that do not embed Markdown in double-quoted shell commands.
- Use safe subprocess and live read-back semantics `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given the helper implementation, when tests inspect the subprocess invocation, then it avoids `shell=True`, uses UTF-8 replacement-safe capture, and performs mutation read-back through live `gh`.
- Cover literal Markdown payloads in tests `[proposed]`
  - Acceptance: Given a test payload with backticks, dollar signs, quotes, and a fenced code block, when the helper builds the GitHub API request, then the serialized body preserves each literal character.

### 2026-06-09-1510-recommend-adding-labels-to-every-issue-created-consumer-or-m: Recommend adding labels to every issue created (consumer or maintainer)  `[completed]`

## Summary

Directive should **recommend** (not mandate) that every issue created — whether by a consumer project's agent or by a directive maintainer — has at least one appropriate label applied at creation time, chosen from the repository's existing label set.

## Rationale

Labels are load-bearing across directive's own workflows:

- **Triage / queue ranking** (`task triage:queue`, refinement, cache-as-authoritative work selection) relies on labels to rank and bucket work.
- The **Issues gauge** in consumer tooling keys off labels (e.g. `blocker` / `P0` / `P1` severity conventions).
- **Triage hygiene / lifecycle reconciliation** treats unlabeled issues as gaps.

An unlabeled issue silently falls out of these flows — it doesn't rank, doesn't surface in the right buckets, and needs a manual follow-up pass to fix.

## Dogfood repro

This was hit immediately: a directive enhancement issue (deftai/directive#1509) was created without labels and required a separate manual step to add `enhancement` / `agent-experience` afterward. A create-time recommendation would have caught it.

## Proposed placement

- At the **issue-creation surfaces** (the skills/flows that file issues during build, review-cycle, triage, and ad-hoc maintainer filing): after creating an issue, check it has >= 1 label and, if not, suggest labels drawn from the repo's existing label set.
- Pull candidate labels from `gh label list` (or the API) — **do not invent new labels ad hoc**; choose from what the repo already defines.

## Recommend, not mandate

Consistent with deftai/directive#1509: this should be a **soft nudge / opt-in** convention, not a hard gate. A maintainer or agent can knowingly create an unlabeled issue; the goal is to make "no labels" a deliberate choice rather than an accident.

## Acceptance (ideas)

- When a directive skill/agent creates an issue, it applies one or more labels selected from the repo's existing label set (or explicitly notes that none applied).
- A triage-hygiene check can surface issues that have no labels for a later sweep.
- Documented explicitly as recommend-not-mandate.

## Relation

Companion to deftai/directive#1509 (project-level changelog/release-notes recommendation). Both are "directive should recommend good project/issue hygiene" items surfaced while dogfooding on `deftai/statusreport`.

**Acceptance**:

- Issue-creation skills recommend existing labels `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given a Directive skill files a GitHub issue, when label guidance is followed, then it recommends selecting at least one appropriate label from the repository's existing label set.
- Guidance does not invent labels or hard-gate issue creation `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given no suitable label is selected, when an issue is created, then the guidance allows an explicit no-label note rather than failing the workflow, and forbids inventing ad hoc labels outside the repo's label set.
- Triage rationale is documented `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given an agent reads the guidance, then it explains that labels feed triage queue ranking, issue gauges, hygiene sweeps, and lifecycle reconciliation.
- Content tests pin the label recommendation `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given content tests run, then they fail if issue-creation skills drop the existing-label recommendation, the no-ad-hoc-label rule, or the recommend-not-mandate language.

### 2026-06-09-1519-bugcheck-consumer-task-check-runs-vendored-framework-self-te: bug(check): consumer task check runs vendored framework self-tests and fails despite clean doctor  `[completed]`

## Summary

In a consumer repository with Deft installed under `.deft/core`, the root `task check` aggregate is not usable as a clean consumer quality gate. It runs the vendored Deft framework's own lint/test/content checks as if the consumer checkout were the Deft source repository, and those framework self-tests fail even when `task doctor -- --full --json` reports a clean install.

This appears to be a Deft Directive tooling/scoping defect, not an application defect in the consumer repo.

## Environment

- Consumer OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Linux arm64
- Deft install layout: vendored payload at `.deft/core`
- Deft version manifest:
  - ref/tag: `v0.41.0`
  - sha: `4f1fdc07a7480a837a84585346dab4ef7738a0ab`
  - install_root: `.deft/core`
- Root Taskfile includes `.deft/core/Taskfile.yml` with `flatten: true`
- Toolchain present:
  - Go: `go1.26.4 linux/arm64`
  - uv: `0.11.19`
  - task: `3.51.1`
  - git: `2.43.0`
  - gh: `2.45.0`
- Doctor result:

```json
{"findings":[{"check":"payload-staleness","message":"no remote sha","severity":"skip","status":"skip"}],"ok":true,"project_root":"/home/parallels/work/site-todo-codex","status":"completed","summary":{"errors":0,"warnings":0}}
```

## Reproduction

From a Deft consumer repo with a clean doctor result and the root Taskfile including the vendored Deft taskfile:

```bash
task doctor -- --full --json
task check
```

## Expected Behavior

In a consumer project, `task check` should either:

1. Run consumer-app gates plus Deft install/structure gates that are valid for a vendored install, or
2. Clearly split framework-source self-tests from consumer checks so the consumer can run a clean quality gate without being responsible for Deft source-repo fixtures and release tests.

A clean `task doctor` should not be followed by a `task check` that fails because framework source-repo tests expect files not deposited in the vendored payload.

## Actual Behavior

`task check` invokes Deft framework checks under `.deft/core` and fails in framework self-tests/content checks. The consumer app's own checks can pass, but the aggregate remains red.

Observed failure classes include:

- `verify:encoding` flags checked-in files inside `.deft/core` for BOM/mojibake/non-ASCII corruption patterns.
- Framework pytest tests fail because they expect Deft source-repo files that are absent in the vendored payload, for example:
  - `.deft/core/.github/workflows/branch-gate.yml`
  - `.deft/core/.gitignore`
  - `.deft/core/.gitattributes`
- Version resolver tests expect mocked `git describe` / fallback values, but installed manifest/version resolution returns the installed payload version `0.41.0`.
- Safety gitignore tests read `.deft/core/.gitignore`, which is absent in this vendored install.

A representative tail from the run:

```text
= 19 failed, 6987 passed, 6 skipped, 9 deselected, 1 xfailed, 6 errors in 27.38s =
task: Failed to run task "check": task: Failed to run task "verify:encoding": exit status 1
```

The run also reports useful gates as passing before the framework-test failure, including vBRIEF validation, strategy-output shape validation, branch protection, toolchain availability, destructive-gh self-test, and SCM boundary checks.

## Consumer Impact

This creates an ambiguous and disruptive quality gate for Deft consumers:

- Application PRs cannot honestly report that global `task check` is clean, even when app-specific tests and Deft lifecycle gates pass.
- Any CI or hook that requires root `task check` may block consumer application work for framework-source-test failures outside the application payload.
- Agents must explain this caveat repeatedly, which lowers trust in the Deft build workflow.
- The failure is especially confusing because `task doctor -- --full --json` reports `ok: true` with zero warnings/errors.

## Why This Should Be Standalone From The Consumer Project

The consumer project is only a reproduction context. The underlying problem is the behavior of Deft's installed/vendored task surface: the aggregate consumer `task check` appears to run framework-source checks that are not valid for the installed payload shape.

## Suggested Fix

Possible approaches:

1. Split aggregate checks by context:
   - `task check` in a consumer repo should run consumer-safe checks only.
   - Framework source-repo self-tests should live behind an explicit target such as `task framework:check` or run only when `.deft/core` is itself the repo root/source checkout.
2. Make framework self-tests install-layout-aware and skip or adapt tests that require source-repo-only files such as `.github/workflows/branch-gate.yml`, `.gitignore`, and `.gitattributes`.
3. Align `task doctor` and `task check` so a clean doctor does not leave the operator with a known-red aggregate check for the same installed payload.
4. Provide a documented consumer app gate target, or deposit a root `task app:check` convention, so application PRs have a clean quality signal distinct from framework payload validation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In a consumer repo with a clean Deft doctor and no application defects, `task check` exits 0 or clearly confines failures to application/consumer-valid gates.
- Framework source-repo tests do not run from a vendored `.deft/core` install unless explicitly requested.
- If any framework install integrity problem exists, `task doctor` and `task check` surface it consistently.
- Documentation/AGENTS guidance clearly tells consumer agents which target is the authoritative pre-commit quality gate.

**Acceptance**:

- Consumer check skips framework source-only tests `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given a vendored .deft/core install in a consumer repo, when task check runs, then framework source-repo tests requiring absent files are not run unless explicitly requested.
- Doctor and check agree on install health `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given task doctor reports a clean install, when task check runs in the same consumer context, then check does not fail for framework payload shape that doctor considers healthy.
- Authoritative consumer quality gate is documented `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given consumer AGENTS/docs guidance names pre-commit checks, then it clearly tells agents which task target is authoritative for consumer application work.
- Regression test covers vendored install shape `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given integration tests simulate a .deft/core vendored install, then they catch task check regressions that run source-only framework tests in the consumer context.

### 2026-06-09-1523-bugdocstemplates-agentsmd-ritual-mainmd-instruct-bare-task-n: bug(docs/templates): AGENTS.md ritual + main.md instruct bare task names that do not resolve under the canonical deft: namespaced include  `[completed]`

## Summary

In a consumer project that follows the **canonical** root-`Taskfile.yml` include pattern documented in `main.md` ("Publishing deft tasks in your project root"), every **bare** `task <name>` command that the generated `AGENTS.md` managed section (and `main.md`) instructs the agent/operator to run fails with:

```
task: Task "<name>" does not exist
```

The canonical include namespaces all deft tasks under `deft:`, so the actually-resolvable names are `task deft:<name>`. But the docs/templates uniformly say `task <name>`. This is an internal inconsistency in directive's own canonical docs, not a consumer misconfiguration.

## Environment

- Consumer: `deftai/statusreport`
- Deft CLI: **v0.42.0** (sha `fffdfad`), `install_root: .deft/core`
- OS: Windows 11, pwsh 7.6.2, Task (go-task) v3, uv
- `task deft:doctor -- --session` → all green (install integrity, `skill-paths-resolve`, `manifest-agreement`, `agents-md-managed-section-fresh`). So this is a healthy, up-to-date install.

## Reproduction

1. Install directive into a consumer project and wire the root `Taskfile.yml` exactly as `main.md` recommends:

   ```yaml
   version: '3'
   includes:
     deft:
       taskfile: ./.deft/core/Taskfile.yml
       optional: true
   ```

2. Start a session and follow the `AGENTS.md` "Session-start ritual (#1149)" verbatim:
   - `task doctor` → `task: Task "doctor" does not exist`
   - `task triage:welcome` → `does not exist`
   - `task verify:cache-fresh` → `does not exist`
3. Prefix with the namespace and every one resolves: `task deft:doctor`, `task deft:triage:welcome`, `task deft:verify:cache-fresh`.

(go-task always exposes an included Taskfile's tasks as `<include-key>:<task>`. With the include key `deft:`, the only resolvable form is `task deft:<task>`. There is no bare form.)

## Root cause — directive's docs are inconsistent with directive's own recommended include

The recommended include namespaces under `deft:`, yet the agent-facing docs reference bare task names throughout:

- **`templates/agents-entry.md`** (source of the consumer `AGENTS.md` managed section) uses bare names everywhere:
  - Session-start ritual (#1149): `task doctor`, `task triage:welcome`, `task verify:cache-fresh`
  - Branch policy: `task verify:branch`, `task policy:show`, `task check`
  - Implementation Intent Gate (#810): `task vbrief:preflight`, `task vbrief:activate`
  - Story Start Gate: `task scope:promote/activate/complete`, `task verify:story-ready`
- **`main.md`** is internally self-contradictory: the "Preferred Workflow: Tasks + Skills Together" section mixes **namespaced** `task deft:issue:ingest` / `task deft:reconcile:issues` (correct) with **bare** `task scope:{...}` / `task roadmap:render` / `task project:render` (broken). The "Migrating from pre-v0.20" section says `task migrate:vbrief` (bare).
- Even the **consumer `Taskfile.yml` comment** that the canonical pattern ships claims the include "surfaces `task spec:render`, `task vbrief:preflight`, `task check`, `task scope:*`, etc. at the project root" — but under the `deft:` namespace those are surfaced as `task deft:spec:render`, `task deft:check`, etc.

## Impact

- Every command in the **mandatory** session-start ritual fails on a by-the-book consumer install until the agent/operator guesses the `deft:` prefix.
- The #810 Implementation Intent Gate and Story Start Gate commands (`task vbrief:preflight`, `task scope:*`, `task verify:story-ready`) all fail as written, so an agent can wrongly conclude the gate is misconfigured / the install is broken.
- Degrades first-session and agent UX and erodes trust in the docs. Related to the consumer-side discoverability concern in #967.

## Suggested fix (apply one direction consistently)

**Option A — make the docs follow the namespace (recommended).** Update `templates/agents-entry.md` and `main.md` to use `task deft:<name>` everywhere, matching the canonical namespaced include (this is already what works for `deft:issue:ingest`). Smallest, lowest-risk change. Also fix the mixed bare/namespaced usage in `main.md`'s Preferred Workflow section and the misleading consumer-`Taskfile.yml` comment.

**Option B — recommend a flatten-able include.** go-task `includes:` always namespaces by key; there is no first-class flatten. Achieving bare names would require top-level alias tasks or a different documented invocation. Heavier and risks name collisions.

**Option C — keep the namespaced include but ship top-level alias tasks** (`doctor`, `check`, `scope:*`, …) in the consumer scaffold that delegate to `deft:*`. Higher maintenance surface.

Recommendation: **Option A**, plus consider a `doctor` check (or a `verify:*` gate) that flags bare `task <name>` references in the managed section so the two surfaces can't silently drift again.

## Related

- #967 — consumer-side `task check` discoverability gap (wire `deft:check` into install-generated scaffolding)
- Prior namespace work (completed): "5 of 11 task namespaces broken for consumer use", "fix triage task aliases", "all task scope commands fail with file not found"

**Acceptance**:

- Managed AGENTS.md uses resolvable consumer task names `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given a consumer install follows the canonical deft: Taskfile include, when the generated AGENTS.md managed section names ritual and gate commands, then those commands use task deft:<name> or clearly distinguish own-repo bare commands.
- main.md no longer mixes bare and namespaced examples `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given a user reads main.md task publishing guidance, then examples consistently match the canonical include namespace and do not claim bare task names are surfaced by that include.
- Content tests prevent namespace drift `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given content tests run, then they fail if consumer-facing ritual or workflow examples reintroduce unresolved bare task names.

### 2026-06-09-1524-bugreleasetriage-lifecycle-sync-gate-reconcile-treat-cancell: bug(release,triage): lifecycle-sync gate + reconcile treat cancelled/ as drift, not a terminal state  `[completed]`

## Summary

The vBRIEF lifecycle-sync release gate (`scripts/release.py::check_vbrief_lifecycle_sync`, #734) and `scripts/reconcile_issues.py --apply-lifecycle-fixes` both treat a `cancelled/` vBRIEF whose GitHub issue is closed as **drift** — i.e. a "closed-issue vBRIEF not in `completed/`" mismatch. This is wrong: `cancelled/` is a legitimate terminal state, distinct from `completed/`.

## Impact

- `task reconcile:issues -- --apply-lifecycle-fixes` **moves** a correctly-cancelled vBRIEF from `cancelled/` -> `completed/`, mislabeling abandoned/duplicate scopes as completed work (and surfacing them as delivered items in ROADMAP/release notes).
- The release Step-3 gate **refuses** to cut a release while any `cancelled/` vBRIEF references a closed issue, forcing operators to either accept the wrong move or pass `--allow-vbrief-drift`.

## Reproduction (2026-06-05 session)

1. Issue #1001 was closed as a duplicate of #1016 (`state_reason=not_planned`); its scope vBRIEF was correctly moved to `xbrief/cancelled/` via `task scope:cancel`.
2. Pre-release `task reconcile:issues -- --apply-lifecycle-fixes` reported `moved=1` and relocated `cancelled/2026-06-05-1001-...xbrief.json` -> `completed/...`.
3. Reverting #1001 back to `cancelled/` makes the release Step-3 gate count it as 1 mismatch and refuse the cut.

## Root cause

`scripts/release.py::check_vbrief_lifecycle_sync` (the mismatch filter):

```python
mismatches = [
    rel for entry in report.get("no_open_issue", [])
    for rel in entry.get("vbrief_files", [])
    if not rel.startswith("completed/")
]
```

The predicate is `not startswith("completed/")`, so `cancelled/` paths are counted as mismatches. `reconcile_issues.py --apply-lifecycle-fixes` shares the same "closed-issue and not in completed/" logic and therefore moves them.

## Expected

- Treat `cancelled/` as a valid terminal state for a closed issue: exclude `cancelled/` (alongside `completed/`) from the mismatch set in both the gate and the apply-mode reconcile.
- A closed-as-`not_planned` / duplicate issue whose vBRIEF is in `cancelled/` should be **clean**, not drift.

## Suggested fix

- In `check_vbrief_lifecycle_sync`, change the predicate to `not (rel.startswith("completed/") or rel.startswith("cancelled/"))`.
- Mirror the same terminal-folder set in `reconcile_issues.py` apply-mode so it never relocates `cancelled/` entries.
- Add regression tests: a closed-issue vBRIEF in `cancelled/` must be (a) not counted by the gate and (b) not moved by apply-mode.

## Workaround used this session

Kept #1001 in `cancelled/` (correct state) and cut the release with `--allow-vbrief-drift`.

**Acceptance**:

- Release gate accepts cancelled terminal state `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given a closed GitHub issue has its vBRIEF in cancelled/, when the release lifecycle-sync gate runs, then it does not count that vBRIEF as drift.
- Reconcile apply-mode does not move cancelled `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given reconcile apply-mode sees a closed issue linked to cancelled/, when fixes are applied, then the vBRIEF stays in cancelled/ and is not relocated to completed/.
- Terminal lifecycle predicate is shared or tested consistently `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given release and reconcile both classify closed-issue lifecycle folders, then tests pin completed/ and cancelled/ as terminal clean states.

### 2026-06-09-1527-scopecomplete-updates-project-definition-references-but-leav: scope:complete updates PROJECT-DEFINITION references but leaves registry item status stale  `[completed]`

## Summary

In a vBRIEF-centric consumer project, `task scope:complete -- <active-scope-vbrief>` moves the scope file to `xbrief/completed/` and updates the `PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` reference URI to point at `completed/...`, but the matching `plan.items[]` registry entry can remain at `status: proposed`.

## Observed behavior

After completing a scope with:

```bash
task scope:complete -- xbrief/active/2026-06-04-sites-membership-api.xbrief.json
```

The lifecycle move succeeded and `PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` references now include:

```json
{
  "uri": "completed/2026-06-04-sites-membership-api.xbrief.json",
  "type": "x-xbrief/plan",
  "title": "Sites and Site Membership API"
}
```

But the corresponding registry item still reads:

```json
{
  "id": "sites-membership-api",
  "title": "Sites and Site Membership API",
  "status": "proposed"
}
```

The same consumer project also had previously completed scope references whose registry items still showed `proposed`, suggesting this is not isolated to one vBRIEF.

## Expected behavior

When lifecycle tooling completes a scope and updates `PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json`, the matching `plan.items[]` entry should either:

- be updated to `status: completed`, or
- be intentionally left alone with a documented validation rule explaining that `plan.items[].status` is not authoritative and may diverge from lifecycle folder/status.

## Impact

Agents and operators can see contradictory project state in the same file: references point at completed scope vBRIEFs, but the scope registry still appears proposed. This makes work selection and dependency reasoning more error-prone unless agents explicitly prefer lifecycle folders over `PROJECT-DEFINITION.plan.items`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `task scope:complete` has deterministic behavior for the matching PROJECT-DEFINITION registry item.
- Either the registry status is synchronized, or docs/validation make the intentional divergence explicit.
- `task vbrief:validate` or a related guard catches unintended stale registry statuses if synchronization is the intended contract.

## Notes

This report is based on consumer-side behavior observed in a vBRIEF v0.6 project using Deft v0.41.0. No project-specific implementation details are needed to reproduce beyond having a PROJECT-DEFINITION registry item matching the completed scope id.

**Acceptance**:

- Scope completion has a registry contract `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given a scope vBRIEF is completed, when PROJECT-DEFINITION contains a matching registry item, then the item status is deterministically synchronized or an explicit validation/docs contract explains divergence.
- References and registry do not contradict unintentionally `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given PROJECT-DEFINITION references point at completed scope vBRIEFs, when validation or project rendering runs, then stale proposed registry statuses are caught or corrected according to the selected contract.
- Regression tests cover consumer project shape `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given a consumer-like vBRIEF project fixture, when task scope:complete runs, then tests assert the registry item outcome and reference rewrite together.

### 2026-06-09-1553-release-document-default-branch-env-bypass-leak-into-nested: release: document default-branch env bypass leak into nested tests  `[completed]`

## Summary

During the v0.43.0 release attempt, using `DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT=1` for the entire `task release` command let the release branch guard pass, but the environment variable leaked into nested `task ci:local` / Go installer tests.

That caused `TestWriteConsumerGitHooks_VendoredCommitBlocked_RealGit` to fail because the vendored test repo inherited the bypass and allowed a direct `master` commit that the test expected the hook to block.

## Why this matters

Future release operators may choose the env-var bypass because the release skill currently names it as an emergency escape hatch for default-branch release commits. For a full release command, that is too broad: it affects child processes and isolated temp repos, producing a false release-preflight failure before any release mutation.

## Desired outcome

Document and/or harden the release workflow so future releases are smoother:

- Prefer the typed direct-commit policy opt-out for release sessions instead of wrapping the whole `task release` invocation in `DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT=1`.
- Warn that the env-var bypass is process-wide and can leak into nested tests or temp repos.
- If the env-var path remains documented, scope it only to narrow branch-guard probes, not to `task release` / `task ci:local`.
- Add content coverage in `tests/content/test_release_workflow.py` so the release skill preserves this guidance.

## Observed failure

`task release -- 0.43.0 --summary ...` stopped at Step 5, before any release mutation:

- preflight git status: OK
- branch == master: OK
- vBRIEF lifecycle sync: OK
- tag availability: OK
- CI preflight: FAIL

Failing test:

`TestWriteConsumerGitHooks_VendoredCommitBlocked_RealGit`

Reason: inherited `DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT=1` caused the vendored pre-commit hook to allow a direct `master` commit.

## Recovery used

No rollback was needed because the pipeline stopped before changelog promotion, tagging, pushing, or release creation. The tree stayed clean and `v0.43.0` did not exist as a tag or GitHub release.

**Acceptance**:

- Release guidance prefers typed policy opt-out `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given an operator needs to release from the default branch, when they read the release skill or release docs, then the guidance prefers the typed direct-commit policy opt-out over wrapping the full task release command in DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT=1.
- Process-wide env bypass warning is explicit `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT remains documented, when the release workflow mentions it, then the text warns that the env var is process-wide and can leak into task ci:local, nested tests, and temporary repositories.
- Content tests pin release bypass guidance `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given tests/content/test_release_workflow.py runs, then it fails if the release workflow drops the typed-policy preference or the warning against broad DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT scoping.

### 2026-06-09-1557-swarm-make-github-credential-policy-runtime-aware-for-local: swarm: make GitHub credential policy runtime-aware for local agents  `[completed]`

## Summary
Local interactive subagents in Cursor/WSL can have valid host GitHub CLI authentication, but the current worker preamble requires an injected `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` and forbids falling back to host `gh` auth. That blocked local swarm workers from creating PRs even though the parent session had `gh auth status` passing and repo access verified.

Grok Build can authorize GitHub inside the agent; Cursor local subagents currently need a different safe path. Directive should distinguish local interactive swarms from cloud/headless workers instead of applying one credential rule everywhere.

## Proposal
Add a runtime-aware GitHub credential mode to the swarm/worker dispatch contract:

- `github_auth_mode: injected-token` for cloud/headless workers. Require `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` (or enterprise equivalents) and fail closed if missing.
- `github_auth_mode: host-gh` for local interactive workers. Permit use of the host `gh` credential store only after preflight confirms `gh auth status`, expected account/repo access, and required scopes.
- Keep tokens out of prompts and transcripts. Do not paste token values into dispatch envelopes.
- Record the selected credential mode in the allocation context or launch manifest so workers know whether host `gh` auth is allowed.

## Acceptance criteria
- Swarm launch or pre-dispatch checks can declare and validate a GitHub auth mode for each worker runtime.
- Local Cursor/Warp/GrokBuild-style agents can use host `gh` auth when a deterministic preflight passes.
- Cloud/headless agents still require injected credentials and do not silently use host state.
- The canonical worker preamble is updated so it forbids host `gh` fallback only for injected-token/cloud mode, not for approved local interactive mode.
- Tests cover missing token in injected-token mode, valid host `gh` auth in local mode, and a repo-access failure in local mode.

## Context
Observed during the WSL maintainer-tooling swarm: one worker completed local implementation but could not create a PR, and another refused to start implementation, because no injected token was present. The parent WSL session had authenticated `gh` and could access `deftai/directive`, but the preamble disallowed host auth fallback.

Refs #1554, #1555.

**Acceptance**:

- Runtime capability probe classifies local-unsandboxed, cursor-native-sandbox, and cloud-headless worker environments. `[proposed]`
- GitHub auth-mode validation runs from the actual worker environment and distinguishes host-gh from injected-token. `[proposed]`
- Swarm allocation context, launch manifest, and worker preamble carry runtime_mode and github_auth_mode consistently. `[proposed]`
- Docs and tests cover Cursor sandbox UID remap, host-gh success, sandbox auth failure, and missing injected-token cloud mode. `[proposed]`

### 2026-06-09-1562-bugtriage-rest-batched-cache-bootstrap-still-spends-minutes: bug(triage): REST-batched cache bootstrap still spends minutes in default local write delay  `[completed]`

## Summary

task triage:bootstrap now uses the REST-paginated cache fetch path, but the default runtime is still much slower than expected because cache_fetch_all keeps the old per-entry delay behavior during the local cache write loop.

A live maintainer run on 2026-06-09 completed successfully but took about 388 seconds. The output showed populate_cache wrote 432 issues and skipped 39 fresh entries. The GitHub retrieve path should only need a handful of REST list pages at per_page=100, so the duration is not explained by remote issue retrieval.

## Observed behavior

- task triage:bootstrap spent several minutes in step 1 populate_cache with no intermediate progress.
- Final recap: issues_written=432 already_fresh=39 issues_failed=0.
- Total elapsed time: about 387.9s.

## Code path checked

- scripts/triage_bootstrap.py delegates to cache.cache_fetch_all.
- scripts/cache.py delegates fetch-all to _cache_fetch.run_fetch_all.
- scripts/_cache_fetch.py uses rest_issue_list_paginated for enumeration, so issue retrieval is REST-paginated rather than per-issue gh issue view.
- scripts/cache.py still sets DEFAULT_DELAY_MS = 500.
- _cache_fetch.run_fetch_all calls _maybe_sleep(delay_ms) after each issue write and again at every batch_size checkpoint.

For 432 writes with the current defaults, the intentional sleep budget alone is roughly (432 + 43) * 0.5s = 237.5s before local JSON rendering, scanning, and disk writes are counted.

## Why this matters

The #1239 REST migration appears to have fixed the remote retrieval shape, but the old pacing defaults still make normal bootstrap feel hung. The UX is especially poor because populate_cache emits only start/done progress, so operators cannot tell whether the job is retrieving, sleeping, scanning, or stuck.

## Suggested fix

- Make the default delay 0 for the REST-paginated path, or only sleep on actual rate-limit/retry paths.
- Add progress inside run_fetch_all for long cohorts, for example every N entries written/skipped.
- Update stale comments/tests that still describe task scm:issue:view as the live implementation path.
- Add a test that protects the production default from reintroducing multi-minute sleeps on REST-batched fetches. Current scale tests pass delay_ms=0, so they do not catch the slow default.

## Acceptance criteria

- A default task triage:bootstrap run for a few hundred open issues no longer spends minutes in intentional local sleeps.
- The cache fetch path remains REST-paginated at per_page=100 and does not regress to per-issue GitHub reads.
- Operators see progress during populate_cache on large cohorts.
- Stale references to task scm:issue:view in this path are corrected or clearly marked historical.

**Acceptance**:

- A default task triage:bootstrap run for a few hundred open issues no longer spends minutes in intentional local sleeps. `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given task triage:bootstrap uses the default cache_fetch_all settings, when the REST-paginated path writes a few hundred issues, then the production default does not add per-entry local sleep delays.
- The cache fetch path remains REST-paginated at per_page=100 and does not regress to per-issue GitHub reads. `[pending]`
  - Acceptance: Given the cache fetch path enumerates issues, when tests run, then they verify rest_issue_list_paginated remains the enumeration path and per-issue gh issue view is not reintroduced.
